title: Programming II
subject: Computer Science and Software

cards.prompt: Define Absolute import dependency. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A specified direct dependency from an importing module to a fully qualified requested module or imported name established by an absolute import operation.
required_concepts: A specified direct dependency from an importing module to a fully qualified requested module or imported name established by an absolute import operation.
major_error_concepts: Using the bound alias as the dependency target identity.

cards.prompt: Define Resolved absolute import name. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The fully qualified module name used by the import machinery after interpreting an absolute request or resolving an explicit relative request against its package anchor.
required_concepts: A resolved absolute import name is the fully qualified module name used by the import machinery.
The name may come directly from an absolute request or from resolution of an explicit relative request.
Resolving an explicit relative request uses its package anchor.
major_error_concepts: Searching the filesystem for the literal dotted-relative spelling.

cards.prompt: What does Python ABC machinery provide? Must an ABC define an abstract member, and does recognition guarantee behavior?
cards.definition: ABCMeta/ABC provides abstract-member instantiation checks and customizable subclass recognition. A class using it may have no abstract members and be instantiable. Registration and subclass hooks can recognize unrelated classes without adding methods or proving behavior.
required_concepts: ABC machinery can prevent instantiation while abstract members remain, but an ABC need not declare any abstract members.
Registration/hooks can recognize classes without implementation inheritance or behavioral proof.
accepted_variants: An ABC may define abstract members, blocking ordinary instantiation until implemented; it may also have none. Virtual registration and hooks can recognize unrelated types but neither adds implementations nor proves behavior.
major_error_concepts: Every ABC must declare an abstract method and only direct or inherited nominal subclasses can be recognized.

cards.prompt: Define Abstract-class instantiation gate. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The runtime restriction preventing ordinary instantiation while unresolved abstract members remain in the effective class, distinct from static checker judgments and behavioral correctness.
required_concepts: The abstract-class instantiation gate prevents ordinary instantiation while unresolved abstract members remain in the effective class.
The gate is a runtime restriction.
The runtime gate is distinct from a static checker's judgment.
Passing the runtime gate does not by itself establish behavioral correctness.
major_error_concepts: Calling successful instantiation proof that the implementation honors the interface semantics.

cards.prompt: Define Abstract method. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A method or descriptor marked as requiring an implementation for ordinary concrete instantiation, while its body may still exist and be callable through cooperative design.
required_concepts: An abstract method is a method or descriptor marked as requiring an implementation for ordinary concrete instantiation.
An abstract method may still have a method body.
An abstract method body may be called through a cooperative design.
The abstract marker governs instantiation rather than proving that the body is absent.
major_error_concepts: Assuming abstract methods must have empty bodies or can never execute.

cards.prompt: Define Module `__all__` export list. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The module-level sequence of names used to define wildcard-export behavior and document an intended surface in some contexts without making names private or validating their existence automatically in every workflow.
required_concepts: A module's `__all__` value is a module-level sequence of export names.
The sequence defines wildcard-export behavior for that module.
The sequence can document an intended public surface in contexts that consult it.
Listing or omitting a name in `__all__` does not make the name private.
`__all__` does not automatically validate every listed name in every workflow.
major_error_concepts: Treating `__all__` as complete access control or universal API enforcement.

cards.prompt: Define Annotation evaluation mode. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The release-bound rules determining when and how annotation expressions are evaluated, stored, deferred, or later resolved, including namespace and import-time failure consequences.
required_concepts: Annotation evaluation mode is bound to a Python release.
The mode determines when and how annotation expressions are evaluated or stored.
The mode determines whether annotations are deferred and how they can later be resolved.
The mode determines which namespace is used during evaluation or resolution.
The mode determines which annotation expressions can cause import-time failure.
major_error_concepts: Assuming all supported Python releases evaluate annotations at the same time and into identical objects.

cards.prompt: Define Python annotation expression. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** Source syntax attached to a variable, parameter, return, or type-related declaration and interpreted under language, evaluation-timing, typing-specification, and checker rules for a specified module.
required_concepts: A Python annotation expression is source syntax attached to a variable, parameter, return, or type-related declaration.
The language version governs how the annotation syntax is interpreted.
The configured evaluation timing governs when an annotation expression is evaluated or deferred.
The typing specification governs its static meaning.
The configured checker governs the analysis result.
All interpretations are scoped to one specified module.
major_error_concepts: Treating every annotation spelling as an already resolved runtime class object.

cards.prompt: Define `Any` propagation edge. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** One assignment, call, return, attribute access, container insertion, or generic substitution through which dynamic `Any` influence reaches another expression or interface under checker rules.
required_concepts: An `Any` propagation edge is one assignment, call, return, attribute access, container insertion, or generic substitution.
Through that edge, dynamic `Any` influence reaches another expression or interface.
The propagation claim is evaluated under the configured checker's rules.
major_error_concepts: Counting only explicit `Any` annotations and missing inferred downstream propagation.

cards.prompt: Define `Any` provenance. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The exact source by which an expression becomes `Any`, such as explicit annotation, untyped definition, missing import, ignored diagnostic, generic omission, or checker inference fallback under the configured configuration.
required_concepts: `Any` provenance records the exact configured reason an expression became `Any`.
The reason may be an explicit annotation, untyped definition, missing import, ignored diagnostic, omitted generic argument, or checker inference fallback.
The provenance is bound to the checker configuration under which it occurred.
major_error_concepts: Reporting only the final `Any` expression while its originating evidence loss remains hidden.

cards.prompt: Define Static `Any` type. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The gradual-typing escape type that permits broad operations and compatibility in both directions under checker rules, suppressing evidence rather than establishing the value's concrete structure or safety.
required_concepts: Static `Any` is a gradual-typing escape type.
Under checker rules, `Any` permits broad operations.
Under checker rules, `Any` permits compatibility in both directions.
Using `Any` suppresses static evidence.
`Any` does not establish the runtime value's concrete structure or safety.
major_error_concepts: Describing `Any` as the top safe type or as a union of all possible types.

cards.prompt: Define API compatibility matrix. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A row-per-declared-consumer comparison across old and new API releases covering imports, signatures, argument binding, state construction, returns, exceptions, effects, protocol or ABC relations, and known unsupported conditions.
required_concepts: An API compatibility matrix has one row for every declared consumer.
Each row compares an identified old API release with an identified new API release.
Each row compares supported imports.
Each row compares callable signatures.
Each row compares argument-binding behavior.
Each row compares state construction.
Each row compares returns and exceptions.
Each row compares side effects.
Each row compares protocol or ABC relations when those relations are part of the consumer contract.
Each row records known unsupported conditions.
major_error_concepts: Calling a change backward compatible because old source still imports.

cards.prompt: Define Declared API consumer. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A named external or cross-module caller class with a specified import path, call pattern, state assumptions, compatibility interval, and observation needs against which one API claim is evaluated.
required_concepts: A declared API consumer is a named external or cross-module class of callers.
The consumer record specifies the import path it uses.
The consumer record specifies its call pattern.
The consumer record specifies relevant state assumptions.
The consumer record specifies the compatibility interval it requires.
The consumer record specifies the observation surfaces it needs.
One API claim is evaluated against those declared consumer conditions.
major_error_concepts: Designing for an abstract user while no actual supported call pattern is recorded.

cards.prompt: Define Public API docstring contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The source-bound documentation of purpose, parameters, return, exceptions, effects, state assumptions, examples, deprecation, and limitations for one public member, kept distinct from executable enforcement.
required_concepts: A public API docstring contract is bound to one public member and its sources.
The docstring states the member's purpose.
The docstring documents parameters.
The docstring documents the return contract.
The docstring documents exceptions.
The docstring documents side effects and state assumptions.
The docstring provides governed examples when examples are part of the contract.
The docstring records deprecation status.
The docstring records limitations.
Documentation remains distinct from executable enforcement of the contract.
major_error_concepts: Treating any triple-quoted string as a complete and current interface contract.

cards.prompt: Define API documentation readback. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The configured tool, import environment, rendered module and member identity, signature, docstring content, warnings, import-time effects, and discrepancies observed from generated documentation lookup.
required_concepts: API documentation readback identifies the configured documentation tool.
The readback identifies the import environment.
The readback identifies the rendered module and member.
The readback records the rendered signature.
The readback records rendered docstring content.
The readback records warnings.
The readback records import-time effects caused during lookup or rendering.
The readback records discrepancies from the declared API contract.
major_error_concepts: Assuming documentation rendering is passive or that successful rendering proves examples and contracts correct.

cards.prompt: Define API exception contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The observed exception types, triggering conditions, timing, payload guarantees, propagation boundaries, and cleanup state that supported callers may rely on.
required_concepts: The observed exception types, triggering conditions, timing, payload guarantees, propagation boundaries, and cleanup state that supported callers may rely on.
major_error_concepts: Listing every exception observed once as permanently supported behavior.

cards.prompt: Define API input contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The accepted argument shapes, value domains, relationships, ownership state, normalization rules, and invalid-input disposition for one specified callable beyond its syntactic signature.
required_concepts: An API input contract specifies accepted argument shapes.
The contract specifies accepted value domains.
The contract specifies required relationships among arguments.
The contract specifies required ownership state for passed objects.
The contract specifies input-normalization rules.
The contract specifies the disposition of invalid inputs beyond what the syntactic signature enforces.
The API input contract is scoped to one specified callable.
major_error_concepts: Treating annotations alone as complete and executed runtime input validation.

cards.prompt: Define API object-ownership contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The declared rights and obligations over mutable inputs, retained references, copied data, returned objects, and resource lifetimes shared between caller and implementation.
required_concepts: An API object-ownership contract states the caller's and implementation's rights over mutable inputs.
The contract states obligations for retained references.
The contract states when data is copied.
The contract states ownership of returned objects.
The contract states responsibility for resource lifetimes.
The ownership rights and obligations define how caller and implementation share mutable state.
major_error_concepts: Saying the API takes data without specifying aliasing and lifetime behavior.

cards.prompt: Define Public API reexport. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A supported binding exposed from one public module or package path whose referenced object is defined or sourced elsewhere, with provenance and compatibility intent recorded.
required_concepts: A public API reexport is a supported binding exposed from a public module or package path.
The object referenced by the binding is defined or sourced elsewhere.
The reexport records the object's provenance.
The reexport records its intended compatibility role.
major_error_concepts: Assuming a reexport creates an independent implementation or automatically tracks reload changes.

cards.prompt: Define Python API contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A Python API contract specifies supported import paths and public objects together with their signatures, accepted inputs, outputs, exceptions, side effects, state assumptions, and compatibility promises for an identified version.
required_concepts: A Python API contract is bound to an identified API version.
The contract specifies supported import paths and public objects.
The contract specifies the signatures of supported public callables.
The contract specifies accepted inputs.
The contract specifies returned outputs.
The contract specifies observable exceptions.
The contract specifies side effects.
The contract specifies state assumptions.
The contract specifies compatibility promises.
major_error_concepts: Versioning implementation files while leaving the consumer-visible interface and behavior unstated.

cards.prompt: Define API return contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified conditions under which a callable returns, the semantic meaning and ownership of its result, ordering and laziness properties, and relation to mutated state or external effects.
required_concepts: An API return contract specifies the conditions under which the callable returns normally.
The contract specifies the semantic meaning of the result.
The contract specifies ownership of the result.
The contract specifies result-ordering properties.
The contract specifies whether result production is lazy.
The contract relates the result to mutated state.
The contract relates the result to external effects.
major_error_concepts: Specifying only a return annotation while result meaning and ownership remain unknown.

cards.prompt: Define API side-effect contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified mutations, stream writes, file or resource access, logs, registrations, callbacks, and external interactions a callable may perform, including ordering and partial-failure boundaries.
required_concepts: An API side-effect contract specifies mutations the callable may perform.
The contract specifies stream writes.
The contract specifies file or resource access.
The contract specifies emitted logs.
The contract specifies registrations and callback invocations.
The contract specifies external interactions.
The contract specifies ordering among observable effects.
The contract specifies which effects may remain after partial failure.
major_error_concepts: Assuming a function is pure because its name sounds like a query or its return type is immutable.

cards.prompt: Define reproducible application execution. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A reproducible application execution binds an identified source tree and environment to an entry point, argument vector, input streams, configuration, external-state policy, logging setup, and observation channels.
required_concepts: A reproducible application execution binds an exact source tree and environment to a selected entry point.
The execution records the ordered argument vector supplied to the entry point.
The execution records the input streams available to the application.
The execution records the resolved configuration used by the application.
The execution declares a policy for external state read or changed by the application.
The execution records the logging setup active during the run.
The execution declares the output and effect channels used to observe the run.
major_error_concepts: Reporting command behavior without fixing the entry point, arguments, configuration, environment, and observation channels.

cards.prompt: Define Application return code. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The integer or agreed status returned by the application entry callable to classify one completed command outcome before any outer process-exit conversion, with meanings documented per command contract.
required_concepts: An application return code is an integer or other agreed status returned by the entry callable.
The command contract assigns outcome meanings to possible return-code values.
The return code exists before an outer launcher converts it to a process exit status.
An application return code is distinct from a diagnostic message or raised exception.
major_error_concepts: Equating any nonzero return with an unhandled Python exception.

cards.prompt: What must an approximate numerical assertion specify, and are all such assertions decimal-place comparisons?
cards.definition: It is an assertion using a declared numerical closeness relation. The framework may use decimal places, absolute tolerance, relative tolerance, ULP distance, or another documented rule. Scale, special-value handling and suitability for the domain must be explicit; frameworks need not use the same rule.
required_concepts: Specify the actual framework's closeness rule, including applicable tolerance and reference scale.
Decimal-place comparison is not universal; relative/absolute rules and special-value policies differ.
accepted_variants: Name the rule and scale, such as pytest.approx's configured relative and absolute tolerances, and handle zero, infinities and NaNs explicitly. An approximate assertion need not round to a fixed number of decimal places.
major_error_concepts: Every approximate assertion accepts numbers only by rounding both to the same decimal place.

cards.prompt: Define argument parser configuration. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** An argument parser configuration is the complete set of parser, command, option, positional, subcommand, default, formatting, and error-policy declarations used to interpret a command-line argument vector.
required_concepts: An argument-parser release records the parser implementation and configuration used by a command.
The release records every declared command and subcommand.
The release records every option and positional declaration.
The release records help and usage formatting behavior.
The release records parse-error behavior and exit handling.
major_error_concepts: Naming a parser library while leaving the active declarations, defaults, or custom behavior unspecified.

cards.prompt: Define process argument vector. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A process argument vector is the ordered sequence of strings supplied to a process after shell parsing, including the program-name element and any empty strings or literal separators.
required_concepts: An argument-vector release is an ordered sequence of strings after the selected shell or launcher has parsed its command text.
The release states whether the program-name element is included in that sequence.
The release preserves empty strings as distinct argument elements.
The release preserves literal separator strings as argument elements when the launcher passes them through.
major_error_concepts: Reconstructing the argument vector from an unquoted shell command after quoting and expansion information has been lost.

cards.prompt: Define Built entry-point metadata readback. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The entry-point groups, names, object references, extras, and distribution provenance extracted from built metadata before installation and compared with project declarations and expected consumer interfaces.
required_concepts: Built entry-point readback extracts entry-point groups, names, and object references from artifact metadata.
The readback retains extras and owning-distribution provenance.
The readback occurs before installation of the artifact.
Extracted records are compared with project declarations and expected consumer interfaces.
major_error_concepts: Treating metadata presence as successful object import or execution.

cards.prompt: Define Distribution artifact member inventory. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The complete normalized archive member paths, sizes, byte hashes, roles, permissions where relevant, and duplicate or unsafe-path observations for one sdist or wheel without executing its contents.
required_concepts: A distribution artifact member inventory records every normalized archive-member path for one sdist or wheel.
The inventory records each member's size, byte hash, and role.
The inventory records relevant permissions for archive members.
The inventory records duplicate names and unsafe path observations.
Inventory inspection does not execute artifact contents.
major_error_concepts: Extracting and importing an unreviewed artifact merely to discover its contents.

cards.prompt: Define Check assertion observation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** One comparison or predicate evaluated by an assertion helper against specified expected and observed values, with comparison semantics, diagnostic representation, and failure control flow preserved.
required_concepts: A check assertion observation evaluates one comparison or predicate.
The assertion compares specified expected and observed values.
The assertion records the comparison semantics used.
The assertion preserves the diagnostic representation of a mismatch.
The assertion preserves the failure control flow produced by the runner.
major_error_concepts: Selecting an assertion for convenient output while its comparison relation mismatches the requirement.

cards.prompt: Define Attribute-lookup trace. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The declared ordered evidence used to resolve `object.name` across object type, descriptors, instance state, class hierarchy, fallback hooks, and possible exception without reducing lookup to one dictionary access.
required_concepts: An attribute-lookup trace is ordered evidence for resolving one specified `object.name` access.
The trace records the object's runtime type.
The trace records applicable descriptor behavior.
The trace records relevant instance state.
The trace records the traversed class hierarchy.
The trace records fallback hooks that were invoked.
The trace records the exception outcome when lookup fails.
The trace does not reduce attribute lookup to a single dictionary access.
major_error_concepts: Searching only the instance dictionary and declaring an attribute absent.

cards.prompt: Define Base interpreter identity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The exact Python executable, implementation, version, build, platform, prefix, configuration, and provenance from which a virtual environment or build context derives its interpreter behavior.
required_concepts: Base interpreter identity records the exact Python executable from which an environment or build context derives interpreter behavior.
The identity records the Python implementation, version, and build.
The identity records the platform and interpreter-prefix configuration.
The identity records provenance for the selected executable and configuration.
major_error_concepts: Naming only Python 3 while the actual executable and implementation remain ambiguous.

cards.prompt: Define Bounded behavioral-substitutability claim. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** Evidence that one candidate implementation can replace another for declared consumers across selected inputs, outputs, exceptions, effects, invariants, performance nonclaims, and state transitions without generalizing beyond the evaluated surface.
required_concepts: A bounded behavioral-substitutability claim is evidence that one candidate implementation can replace another for declared consumers.
The evidence covers selected inputs.
The evidence covers returned outputs.
The evidence covers observable exceptions.
The evidence covers side effects.
The evidence covers required invariants.
The evidence records performance nonclaims.
The evidence covers state transitions.
The conclusion does not generalize beyond the evaluated consumer and observation surface.
major_error_concepts: Inferring substitutability from shared inheritance, ABC registration, or protocol conformance alone.

cards.prompt: Define Bound instance method. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The callable produced when a function descriptor is accessed through an instance, retaining the instance for implicit first-argument binding while preserving the underlying function identity separately.
required_concepts: A bound instance method is produced when a function descriptor is accessed through an instance.
The result is callable.
The bound method retains the accessed instance.
The retained instance is supplied through implicit first-argument binding.
The underlying function's identity remains separately observable.
major_error_concepts: Treating a bound method as a copied function stored independently on each instance.

cards.prompt: Define Bounded type parameter. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A type parameter restricted to subtypes assignable to one upper-bound type while preserving the concrete inferred subtype in generic results where specification rules allow.
required_concepts: A bounded type parameter is restricted to types assignable to one declared upper-bound type.
Checker inference can preserve the concrete subtype selected for the parameter in generic results.
Concrete-subtype preservation is limited to cases allowed by the typing specification.
major_error_concepts: Treating an upper bound as a fixed replacement type that erases the chosen subtype.

cards.prompt: Define Breaking public-import change. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A specified change that makes a previously supported import path, name, or initialization behavior unavailable or observably incompatible for at least one declared consumer condition.
required_concepts: A breaking public-import change is evaluated against a previously supported import path, public name, or initialization behavior.
The change makes that supported behavior unavailable or observably incompatible.
At least one declared consumer condition must be affected.
The breaking-change claim is limited to the specified consumer and release conditions.
major_error_concepts: Claiming compatibility solely because the implementation still exists at a different path.

cards.prompt: Define Build-backend object reference. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The pyproject string identifying the importable backend object that implements standardized build hooks, interpreted within the build environment and kept distinct from its providing distribution name.
required_concepts: A build-backend reference is the pyproject string naming an importable backend object.
The named object implements standardized build hooks.
The reference is interpreted within the provisioned build environment.
The backend's import reference is distinct from the distribution name that provides it.
major_error_concepts: Calling the backend reference a shell command or package-index project name.

cards.prompt: Describe a Python build frontend and distinguish its role from optional build isolation.
cards.definition: A build frontend selects source, invokes backend hooks, collects artifacts and reports failures. It usually provisions an isolated environment containing build requirements; a configured non-isolated mode instead uses an existing environment. The backend remains responsible for project-specific build behavior.
required_concepts: The frontend orchestrates backend hooks, artifacts and failures rather than defining all project build semantics.
Isolation is a configurable environment strategy, not a defining requirement of being a frontend.
accepted_variants: It orchestrates the backend and collects results. python -m build --no-isolation still uses a build frontend, but build requirements must already be supplied in its environment.
major_error_concepts: A tool is not a build frontend whenever --no-isolation prevents creation of a new build environment.

cards.prompt: What is a build-system requirement, and where must it be available with and without build isolation?
cards.definition: It is a dependency needed to provision and invoke a project's build backend. With isolation enabled, the frontend supplies build requirements in its build environment; without isolation they must be made available in the selected existing environment. Build requirements are distinct in role from runtime dependencies.
required_concepts: Build-system requirements enable the build backend, not ordinary application execution by definition.
Their environment depends on the chosen isolation mode; they must still be available if isolation is disabled.
accepted_variants: They supply the backend and its build-time needs. Isolation usually provisions them separately; --no-isolation uses existing installed build dependencies. They are not automatically the project's runtime dependencies.
major_error_concepts: Build-system requirements exist only in isolated builds, so disabling isolation removes the need for them.

cards.prompt: Define Build source selection. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The backend- and configuration-dependent decision over which packages, modules, resources, metadata, and other files enter an sdist or wheel, verified through artifact inventories rather than source-tree presence.
required_concepts: Build source selection is the backend-dependent and configuration-dependent choice of content included in an sdist or wheel.
The choice may cover packages, modules, resources, metadata, and other files.
Artifact-member inventories verify the result of source selection.
A file's presence in the source tree does not establish its inclusion in a built artifact.
major_error_concepts: Assuming every repository file is included in every built artifact.

cards.prompt: Define `build-system` table. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The pyproject table declaring minimum build requirements and the build-backend object reference used by a frontend to provision and invoke a project build under standardized interfaces.
required_concepts: The build-system table declares minimum requirements for provisioning the build environment.
The table declares the build-backend object reference invoked by a build frontend.
The frontend interprets the table through standardized build interfaces.
major_error_concepts: Assuming project runtime dependencies also install the build backend automatically.

cards.prompt: Define Built-in configuration default. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A source-controlled application value selected when no higher-precedence valid source overrides it, with type, semantic meaning, release identity, and distinction from parser defaults explicit.
required_concepts: A built-in configuration default is a source-controlled value selected when no higher-precedence valid source supplies the field.
The default declaration specifies the value's type and application meaning.
The default is bound to the application release that contains its declaration.
A built-in configuration default is distinct from a parser default that may obscure source provenance.
major_error_concepts: Treating equal values from different sources as identical provenance.

cards.prompt: Define Built distribution metadata readback. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The name, version, Python requirement, dependencies, optional groups, entry points, and other standardized fields read from built artifact metadata and reconciled against static and dynamic project declarations.
required_concepts: Built metadata readback extracts the distribution name, version, and Python requirement from an artifact.
The readback extracts dependencies, optional groups, and entry points.
The readback extracts other standardized fields relevant to the release contract.
Extracted values are reconciled against static and dynamic project declarations.
major_error_concepts: Reading pyproject alone and claiming it equals finalized artifact metadata.

cards.prompt: Define Bounded call-graph edge. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A caller-site-to-callee or candidate relation annotated with source release, static resolution basis, runtime observation, argument shape, condition, wrapper behavior, and unresolved dispatch alternatives.
required_concepts: A bounded call-graph edge links a caller site to a callee or candidate callee.
The edge records the source release and static resolution basis.
The edge records runtime observation, argument shape, and execution condition.
The edge records wrapper behavior and unresolved dispatch alternatives.
major_error_concepts: Presenting a static call graph as exact executed control flow.

cards.prompt: Define callable signature. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A callable signature records the ordered parameters, their kinds, defaults, and annotations, together with the return annotation and the binding rules exposed by a callable.
required_concepts: A callable signature records parameters in their binding order.
The signature records each parameter's kind.
The signature records each parameter's default when one exists.
The signature records parameter annotations.
The signature records the return annotation.
The signature exposes the argument-binding rules for the callable.
major_error_concepts: Reducing a callable signature to its argument count or type names while ignoring parameter kind, order, defaults, and binding behavior.

cards.prompt: Define Callable call site. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A specified expression that can invoke a callable after evaluating receiver, arguments, dynamic lookup, and dispatch, linked to confirmed or candidate callees with static and runtime evidence distinguished.
required_concepts: A callable call site is a specified expression that can invoke a callable after receiver and arguments are evaluated.
The site record accounts for dynamic lookup and dispatch.
The site links to confirmed callees or conservative candidate callees.
Static call evidence remains distinct from runtime-observed invocation evidence.
major_error_concepts: Resolving every attribute call to one callee from spelling alone.

cards.prompt: Define Public callable identity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The supported qualified import path, defining object identity, callable kind, frozen signature, and compatibility status of one function, bound method, class, or callable object.
required_concepts: Public callable identity records the supported qualified import path.
Public callable identity records the defining object's identity.
Public callable identity records whether the object is a function, bound method, class, or other callable object.
Public callable identity records a frozen signature.
Public callable identity records the callable's compatibility status.
major_error_concepts: Identifying a callable only by its unqualified function name.

cards.prompt: Define Public callable contract table. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The reconciled identity, consumer, signature, binding examples, input domain, return, exceptions, effects, ownership, laziness, compatibility, and nonclaim fields for every supported callable in an API release.
required_concepts: A public callable contract table covers every supported callable in one API release.
Each row records callable identity and declared consumers.
Each row records the supported signature.
Each row records argument-binding examples.
Each row records the accepted input domain.
Each row records the return contract.
Each row records exceptions.
Each row records side effects.
Each row records ownership and laziness obligations.
Each row records compatibility status.
Each row records explicit nonclaims.
major_error_concepts: Publishing generated signatures alone as complete and current callable documentation.

cards.prompt: Define Callable signature inspection. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified attempt to obtain parameter kinds, names, defaults, annotations, return annotation, wrapper adjustments, and failure limitations for a runtime callable through documented inspection interfaces.
required_concepts: Callable signature inspection attempts to obtain parameter kinds, names, defaults, and annotations for one runtime callable.
The inspection attempts to obtain the return annotation.
The inspection records signature adjustments introduced by wrappers.
The inspection records failures and limitations of the documented inspection interface.

cards.prompt: Define Command-line interface contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified command and subcommand names, argument grammar, meanings, defaults, validation, configuration relations, outputs, diagnostics, return codes, side effects, and compatibility promises supported for external invocation.
required_concepts: A command contract declares the command and subcommand names accepted by an application.
The contract declares the accepted argument grammar.
The contract assigns meanings to accepted arguments.
The contract declares defaults for omitted arguments.
The contract declares validation rules for parsed values.
The contract declares how command arguments relate to other configuration sources.
The contract declares the application's output formats and diagnostic behavior.
The contract assigns meanings to return codes and observable side effects.
The contract states compatibility commitments for command consumers.
major_error_concepts: Treating an example invocation as the complete supported command grammar.

cards.prompt: Define Command argument default. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The parser-supplied value or absence behavior used when a declaration receives no matching vector input, kept distinct from application configuration defaults and conversion of explicit values.
required_concepts: A command default is the parser value or absence produced when the associated argument is not supplied.
The command default is distinct from an application-level default applied after parsing.
The declaration states whether explicit input is converted differently from the stored default.
major_error_concepts: Calling a parser default the provenance of every effective application value.

cards.prompt: Define Parsed argument destination. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The parser-result attribute or mapping key receiving a converted value from one or more declarations, with naming, collisions, defaults, and suppressed-storage behavior recorded.
required_concepts: A command destination is the result attribute or mapping key that receives a converted value from one or more argument declarations.
The destination declaration records how the result attribute or mapping-key name is chosen.
The parser contract states how destination-name collisions are resolved.
The parser contract states how defaults populate the destination.
The parser contract states when destination storage is suppressed.
major_error_concepts: Inferring result field names only from displayed option strings.

cards.prompt: Define Command domain validation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** Application or parser logic checking semantic relationships beyond token grammar and basic conversion, with invalid-value disposition, diagnostic channel, return code, and side-effect ordering explicit.
required_concepts: Command-domain validation checks semantic constraints beyond argument grammar and type conversion.
The validation contract identifies each rejected value or cross-argument relation.
The validation contract identifies the diagnostic channel and process outcome for rejection.
The validation contract specifies whether any application side effect may occur before rejection.
major_error_concepts: Assuming successful parsing establishes every cross-field and environmental precondition.

cards.prompt: Define Command flag action. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** An option-triggered parser action that sets, clears, counts, appends, or otherwise updates a destination without necessarily consuming a separate value token, with repeated-use semantics explicit.
required_concepts: A command-flag action defines the state change caused by the presence of a declared option.
A flag action may set a value, clear a value, count occurrences, append a value, or perform another declared action.
Some flag actions consume no following value from the argument vector.
The action declaration specifies how repeated flag appearances affect the destination.
major_error_concepts: Treating every option as consuming exactly one following argument.

cards.prompt: Define Command help contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified usage, positional and optional argument descriptions, defaults where exposed, subcommand list, examples, exit behavior, and limitation text presented by parser-generated or custom help.
required_concepts: A command-help contract specifies the usage text shown for the command.
The help contract describes positional and optional arguments.
The help contract states which defaults are exposed to users.
The help contract describes available subcommands and representative examples.
The help contract specifies the stream and exit behavior for help requests.
The help contract states known limitations of the displayed documentation.
Command help may be generated by the parser or supplied by custom help logic.
major_error_concepts: Treating successful help rendering as proof every documented invocation works.

cards.prompt: Define Command parse failure. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A configured parser rejection caused by unrecognized, missing, malformed, conflicting, or choice-invalid argument input, with diagnostic text, usage emission, exception behavior, streams, and exit status recorded.
required_concepts: A command parse failure rejects an argument vector under the parser contract.
Rejection may result from an unrecognized, missing, malformed, conflicting, or disallowed argument.
The failure contract specifies the diagnostic and usage text produced on rejection.
The failure contract specifies any exception raised and the streams used for reporting.
The failure contract specifies the resulting process exit behavior.
major_error_concepts: Reporting every nonzero command exit as a parse failure.

cards.prompt: What does Command stderr-stream contract diagnose or distinguish?
cards.definition:
**Definition.** The recorded process stderr stream for parse messages, application errors, warnings, or logs as configured, with format stability and separation from statistical standard error, exception objects, and process status explicitly bounded.

**Worked check.** A CLI writes diagnostics to stderr and data to stdout; capture both streams separately so a successful data pipeline cannot parse an error line as output.
required_concepts: Command standard error is the recorded diagnostic stream used for selected parse errors, application errors, warnings, or logs.
The command contract specifies which diagnostics are written to standard error and their format stability.
Command standard error is distinct from a statistical standard error.
Command standard error is distinct from an exception object and from the process exit status.
major_error_concepts: Treating stderr output as automatically indicating a nonzero exit or failed command.

cards.prompt: Define Command standard-output contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified user- or pipeline-facing text or bytes written to standard output, including format, ordering, terminators, stability, partial-output behavior, and separation from diagnostic logging.
required_concepts: Command standard output carries user-facing or pipeline-facing text or bytes produced by the application.
The command contract specifies standard-output format, ordering, and record terminators.
The command contract specifies which standard-output details are stable for consumers.
The command contract specifies whether partial standard output can precede a failure.
Standard output remains distinct from diagnostic logging unless the contract intentionally combines them.
major_error_concepts: Mixing debug logs into a promised machine-readable output stream.

cards.prompt: Define Command argument type conversion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The parser invocation of a declared conversion callable on selected argument strings, producing a value or parse-classified failure while retaining callable identity, input text, effects, and exception behavior.
required_concepts: Command type conversion applies a declared conversion callable to an argument string.
A successful conversion supplies the value stored for that argument.
A declared conversion failure becomes a parse failure under the parser contract.
The conversion record preserves callable identity, input text, side effects, and exception behavior.
major_error_concepts: Treating a type annotation on application code as argparse conversion.

cards.prompt: Define Command usage line. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The concise parser-rendered or custom syntax summary for one command branch, interpreted as documentation rather than a complete formal grammar or execution receipt.
required_concepts: A command usage line is a concise parser-rendered or custom notation for one command-syntax branch.
The usage line is documentation rather than a complete formal grammar.
The usage line is not evidence that the depicted invocation executed successfully.
major_error_concepts: Inferring every cardinality and semantic constraint from the usage line alone.

cards.prompt: Function f moves from module old to module new, but old is supported for one deprecation window. What binding, two import-path checks, and removal condition provide a compatibility reexport?
cards.definition: Retain an old-path binding, such as from new import f inside old. Check that both old.f and new.f import and satisfy the supported callable contract, using controlled fresh imports when initialization matters. Remove the bridge only under the announced deprecation/removal policy after the promised window and required migration conditions.
required_concepts: Retain the old import binding to the relocated supported object.
Check both old and new import routes and their promised behavior.
Gate removal on the stated deprecation window and migration/removal policy.
accepted_variants: Keep from new import f in old, verify both old.f and new.f through the supported imports and behavior checks, and remove old.f only when the announced window and removal conditions are satisfied.
major_error_concepts: A reexport means move f to new, delete old immediately, and check only that new imports.

cards.prompt: Define Change compatibility-risk record. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The affected consumer, relied-upon contract field, old and new behavior, evidence strength, severity, likelihood boundary, migration or compatibility candidate, and unresolved external-consumer uncertainty for one proposed change.
required_concepts: A compatibility-risk record identifies the affected consumer and relied-upon contract field.
The record compares old and proposed behavior.
The record states evidence strength, severity, and the boundary of likelihood estimation.
The record identifies a migration or compatibility candidate when one is supported.
The record retains uncertainty about unobserved external consumers.
major_error_concepts: Assigning one risk level to an entire file change with no consumer relation.

cards.prompt: Define Object composition relation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A specified object or component retaining and delegating to another object through an explicit field or constructor dependency rather than inheriting its implementation identity.
required_concepts: Object composition retains another object through an explicit field or constructor dependency.
The composing object delegates selected behavior to the retained object.
Composition does not inherit the retained object's implementation identity.
major_error_concepts: Calling any local object creation composition without recording ownership and delegation boundaries.

cards.prompt: Define Conditional import. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** An import request reached only when a specified branch, platform, version, type-checking, or other runtime condition selects its containing path.
required_concepts: An import request reached only when a specified branch, platform, version, type-checking, or other runtime condition selects its containing path.
major_error_concepts: Reporting conditional availability as unconditional support across the entire project.

cards.prompt: Define Application configuration schema. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified keys, nested structure, expected runtime value kinds, optionality, defaults, allowed unknown-key policy, relationships, and error dispositions required after source parsing.
required_concepts: A configuration schema declares accepted keys and their nested structure.
The schema declares the value kinds and optionality of configuration fields.
The schema declares field defaults and the policy for unknown keys.
The schema declares required relationships among multiple fields.
The schema declares the errors produced for invalid configuration shapes or values.
major_error_concepts: Using TOML parse success alone as complete application schema validation.

cards.prompt: Define Effective configuration validation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The schema and cross-field checks applied to resolved values before application work, with rejected fields, source provenance, diagnostics, return status, and absence of unauthorized side effects recorded.
required_concepts: Configuration-domain validation applies field and cross-field constraints after configuration assembly.
Validation occurs before application work that depends on the configuration.
A rejection identifies the invalid field relationship and its source provenance.
A rejection specifies the diagnostic and application return status.
A rejected configuration causes no unauthorized application side effects.
major_error_concepts: Validating each source independently while an invalid combination emerges only after precedence.

cards.prompt: Define Configuration precedence rule. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified field-specific order and merge or replacement semantics among built-in, file, environment, command, and other authorized sources, including invalid-source behavior and provenance retention.
required_concepts: A configuration precedence rule orders built-in, file, environment, command, and other declared sources for each field.
The rule specifies merge or replacement behavior when multiple sources supply a field.
The rule specifies the disposition of invalid values from a candidate source.
The rule preserves provenance for the winning and shadowed candidate values.
major_error_concepts: Saying CLI wins without defining absent values, nested merging, or invalid overrides.

cards.prompt: Define effective application configuration. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** Effective application configuration is the validated result of combining defaults, configuration files, environment values, and command-line overrides according to declared precedence and provenance rules.
required_concepts: A configuration release is the validated configuration selected for one application execution.
The release may combine built-in defaults, configuration files, process-environment values, and command arguments.
The release records the precedence and merge rules used to combine sources.
The release records the provenance of every effective configuration value.
major_error_concepts: Recording only final values while losing which source supplied or overrode each value.

cards.prompt: Define Installed console-command readback. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The target-environment command path, generated wrapper provenance, argument vector, loaded entry object, configuration, stdout, stderr, logs, return, process exit, and side effects for one installed console-script execution.
required_concepts: Installed console-command readback identifies the target-environment command path and generated-wrapper provenance.
The readback records the argument vector and loaded entry object.
The readback records the resolved application configuration.
The readback records standard output, standard error, and log observations.
The readback records the application return, process exit status, and observable side effects.
major_error_concepts: Calling metadata discovery proof that the generated console command works.

cards.prompt: What metadata maps a Python installed console command to an entry callable, and what does that declaration not prove?
cards.definition: A [project.scripts] entry maps a command name to an object reference, producing an entry in the console_scripts group. Installers use that metadata to provide platform-appropriate command integration. The declaration alone does not prove the referenced callable imports or runs successfully.
required_concepts: Map command name to object reference through project.scripts/console_scripts metadata.
Installed command execution and callable validity still require separate checks.
accepted_variants: [project.scripts] can map hello to pkg.cli:main; it becomes a console_scripts entry. The installer supplies command integration, but metadata alone does not demonstrate a successful import or run.
major_error_concepts: The standardized entry-point group is console-scripts, and merely listing the command proves its callable executes.

cards.prompt: Define Constrained type parameter. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A type parameter whose solutions are limited to one of a declared finite set of types under checker inference, differing from an upper bound and from an arbitrary union parameter.
required_concepts: A constrained type parameter has solutions limited to a declared finite set of types.
The configured checker selects among those solutions during inference.
A finite constraint set is distinct from a single upper bound.
A constrained type parameter is distinct from an arbitrary union-typed parameter.
major_error_concepts: Assuming constraints preserve every concrete subtype exactly like an upper bound.

cards.prompt: Define Constructor-supplied dependency. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A required collaborator provided during instance construction under a declared callable or protocol contract, ownership rule, lifetime, and failure policy.
required_concepts: A required collaborator provided during instance construction under a declared callable or protocol contract, ownership rule, lifetime, and failure policy.
major_error_concepts: Passing a collaborator without defining which methods or behavior the consumer requires.

cards.prompt: Define Contravariant consumer interface. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A generic interface using a type parameter in input-compatible positions so a consumer able to accept a supertype can be assignable where a consumer of the subtype is expected.
required_concepts: A contravariant consumer uses its type parameter in input-compatible positions.
A consumer that accepts a supertype can then be assignable where a consumer of the subtype is expected.
Contravariant-consumer assignability remains subject to the declared generic and checker rules.
major_error_concepts: Reversing the assignability direction because the word subtype appears in the requested interface.

cards.prompt: Define Control-flow static type state. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The checker-inferred types and reachability facts associated with bindings at one source program point after accounting for preceding branches, assignments, exits, assertions, and exceptional control under a recorded analysis.
required_concepts: Control-flow static type state records inferred binding types at one source program point.
The state records reachability facts at that point.
The state accounts for preceding branches.
The state accounts for preceding assignments.
The state accounts for preceding exits and assertions.
The state accounts for exceptional control flow.
The state is bound to one recorded checker analysis.
major_error_concepts: Assigning one global inferred type to a variable across every control-flow location.

cards.prompt: Define Controlled code change. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A versioned edit limited to the declared contract or implementation mechanism while unrelated formatting, dependencies, tools, fixtures, configuration, and environment remain fixed enough for before-after attribution.
required_concepts: A controlled code change is a versioned edit limited to the declared contract or implementation mechanism.
Unrelated formatting, dependencies, tools, fixtures, and configuration remain fixed enough for comparison.
The execution environment remains fixed enough to attribute observed differences to the declared edit.
major_error_concepts: Combining structural refactor, dependency updates, and behavior changes into one impact experiment.

cards.prompt: Define Covariant producer interface. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A generic interface using a type parameter in output-compatible positions so an instance producing a subtype can be assignable where a producer of the supertype is expected under specified rules.
required_concepts: A covariant producer uses its type parameter in output-compatible positions.
A producer of a subtype can then be assignable where a producer of the supertype is expected.
Covariant-producer assignability remains subject to the declared generic and checker rules.
major_error_concepts: Declaring covariance on an interface that also accepts arbitrary values of the same parameter type.

cards.prompt: Define Circular-import failure mechanism. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The specific active initialization path, recursive request, cache hit, requested binding, and missing-or-stale state that connects an import-cycle component to a specified failure.
required_concepts: A circular-import failure mechanism identifies the active module-initialization path.
The mechanism identifies the recursive import request on that path.
The mechanism identifies the relevant module-cache hit.
The mechanism identifies the binding requested from the partially initialized module.
The mechanism identifies the missing or stale state observed at that point.
The traced initialization facts connect an import-cycle component to one specified runtime failure.
major_error_concepts: Repairing arbitrary import syntax without identifying the order-sensitive unavailable state.

cards.prompt: Define Circular-import repair candidate. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A bounded change to dependency direction, shared interface placement, import timing, or public surface predicted to remove the specified partial-initialization mechanism with compatibility effects stated.
required_concepts: A circular-import repair candidate is a bounded change to dependency direction, shared-interface placement, import timing, or the public surface.
The candidate predicts how that change removes the specified partial-initialization mechanism.
The candidate states the resulting compatibility effects.
major_error_concepts: Moving an import inside a function and calling the design repaired without evaluating repeated runtime behavior and dependencies.

cards.prompt: Define `python -m` module execution. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** Import-system location of a qualified module or package followed by execution in the initial top-level environment while retaining package-aware metadata needed by relative imports.
required_concepts: `python -m` execution asks the import system to locate a qualified module or package.
The selected code is then executed in the initial top-level environment.
The execution retains package-aware metadata.
The retained package metadata supports explicit relative imports.
major_error_concepts: Describing `-m` as merely opening a path with an alternative spelling.

cards.prompt:
What does P('bad') produce here, and does x: int enforce the value's runtime type?
```python
from dataclasses import dataclass
@dataclass
class P:
    x: int
    y: int = 0
```
cards.definition: The default dataclass options generate initialization, representation and field equality where not overridden. P('bad') stores the string in x and 0 in y; its ordinary representation is P(x='bad', y=0). Dataclass field annotations are not runtime type validators. It remains a Python class with normal user methods and inheritance.
required_concepts: The generated initializer accepts 'bad' as x and supplies y=0; the representation exposes those field values.
The int annotation itself does not reject the string at runtime.
accepted_variants: P('bad') gives fields x='bad' and y=0, represented as P(x='bad', y=0). dataclass does not enforce the int annotation.
major_error_concepts: P('bad') raises a type error automatically because dataclass enforces x: int at runtime.

cards.prompt: Two Bag instances omit a mutable items field. Which dataclass declaration gives each its own list, and what identity test verifies that?
cards.definition: Declare items: list[int] = field(default_factory=list) in a dataclass. The zero-argument list factory is invoked for each omitted value during generated initialization. For a=Bag() and b=Bag(), (a.items is b.items) evaluates to False. A general factory is not guaranteed to return distinct objects unless its behavior does so.
required_concepts: Use field(default_factory=list) or an equivalent zero-argument factory that creates a fresh list per instance.
Check (a.items is b.items) is False, not merely value equality.
accepted_variants: Use items: list[int] = field(default_factory=list). For a=Bag() and b=Bag(), (a.items is b.items) evaluates to False; equality of their initially empty contents would not test aliasing.
major_error_concepts: Use field(default_factory=list()) or one shared list object and verify only a.items == b.items.

cards.prompt: Define Dataclass generated equality. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** Dataclass-generated equality compares fields with compare=True in declaration order only when the other object has the identical runtime type; it is distinct from identity, hashing, ordering, and domain equivalence.
required_concepts: Dataclass-generated equality compares fields whose `compare` option is true.
Dataclass-generated equality compares the selected fields in declaration order.
Generated equality requires the other object to have the identical runtime type.
Generated equality is distinct from object identity.
Generated equality is distinct from hashing and generated ordering.
Generated equality does not by itself establish domain-specific equivalence.
major_error_concepts: Calling generated field equality a complete semantic domain-equivalence proof.

cards.prompt: What does a dataclass field describe, and do all fields appear as initializer parameters or have defaults?
cards.definition: A dataclass field records a declared data attribute and options controlling generated behavior. Its metadata can govern initialization, representation, comparison, keyword-only status and a default or factory when present. init=False omits it from generated initializer parameters, and required fields can have no default.
required_concepts: A field describes a data attribute plus options governing generated dataclass behavior.
Not every field has an initializer parameter or default: init=False and required no-default fields are valid.
accepted_variants: A field describes a data attribute plus generation options such as init, repr, compare and kw_only. init=False can remove its constructor parameter; a required field can have no default at all.
major_error_concepts: Every dataclass field must become an __init__ parameter and must record a default or default_factory.

cards.prompt: What does dataclass order=True generate, which objects can it compare, and what option conflicts matter?
cards.definition: With order=True, dataclass generates lexicographic ordering over comparison-enabled fields in declaration order. Both operands must have identical runtime type for this generated comparison. order=True requires eq=True; defining an ordering method while also requesting generated ordering raises an error. Field order is not automatically a meaningful domain order.
required_concepts: Generated ordering is lexicographic over selected fields and requires identical operand types.
order=True with eq=False is invalid; conflicts with user-defined ordering methods are invalid.
accepted_variants: It compares selected fields lexicographically for identical types, not arbitrary base/subclass pairs. order=True needs eq=True and cannot coexist with explicit ordering methods.
major_error_concepts: Generated ordering treats every subclass instance as interchangeable with a base instance and works with order=True, eq=False.

cards.prompt: Define Dataclass post-initialization hook. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The optional method called by a generated initializer after generated field assignments, available for derived state or validation while retaining partial-state and exception effects.
required_concepts: A dataclass post-initialization hook is an optional method called by a generated initializer.
The call occurs after generated field assignments.
The hook can compute derived state or validate the initialized state.
The hook contract accounts for partially initialized state.
The hook contract accounts for effects that remain when the hook raises an exception.
major_error_concepts: Assuming the hook runs when a user-defined initializer replaces the generated call path.

cards.prompt: Define Dataclass replacement construction. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** Creation of a new dataclass instance by supplying selected changed fields through the class's initialization path, with post-init behavior, non-init fields, and shallow referenced-object sharing considered.
required_concepts: Dataclass replacement constructs a new instance.
Selected changed fields are supplied through the class's initialization path.
Replacement accounts for post-initialization behavior.
Replacement accounts for fields excluded from generated initialization.
Unchanged referenced objects may remain shallowly shared between the old and new instances.
major_error_concepts: Calling replacement a deep immutable update with no constructor effects.

cards.prompt: What boundary or limitation does Dependency declaration-resolution boundary impose?
cards.definition:
**Definition.** The explicit separation among requirement declarations, marker evaluation, candidate discovery, resolver decisions, downloaded artifacts, installed distributions, import availability, and observed compatibility.

**Worked check.** A type checker can resolve an imported annotation from stubs while runtime import execution still fails; record which resolver and environment produced each result.
required_concepts: The dependency declaration-resolution boundary separates requirement declarations from marker evaluation.
The boundary separates candidate discovery from resolver decisions and downloaded artifacts.
The boundary separates installed distributions from import availability.
The boundary separates all preceding packaging evidence from observed compatibility of executed behavior.
major_error_concepts: Calling valid dependency metadata a successfully resolved and installed environment.

cards.prompt: Define default argument object. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A Python default expression is evaluated once when the function definition executes and the resulting object is stored with the function; on a call that omits the argument, that stored object is bound to the parameter, so mutable defaults are shared across such calls.
required_concepts: A Python default expression is evaluated once when the function definition executes.
The resulting default object is stored with the function.
When a call omits the argument, the stored object is bound to the parameter.
A mutable stored default is therefore shared across calls that omit that argument.
major_error_concepts: Treating a default expression as if Python reevaluated it automatically on every call.

cards.prompt: What can change when an import is moved inside a later call, and is module initialization necessarily postponed?
cards.definition: Deferral moves when that import request is reached. It can delay first initialization and failures if the module is not already loaded; if another path has initialized it, the deferred request may simply hit the cache. Repeated request cost, dependency visibility and static annotation needs must still be considered.
required_concepts: Separate the delayed request from first module initialization, which might already have happened elsewhere.
Describe possible failure-timing, repeated lookup and visibility/type-checking tradeoffs.
accepted_variants: The request occurs later. First initialization is delayed only if no earlier path loads the module; otherwise the request can be a cache hit. Failure timing, repeated lookup overhead, dependency visibility and annotation needs can change.
major_error_concepts: Moving an import into a function guarantees that no other path can initialize its module before that function runs.

cards.prompt: Define Definition reference. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A specified source or generated occurrence resolved or conservatively linked to a qualified definition through syntax, name binding, import, attribute access, type information, or runtime identity, with confidence and ambiguity recorded.
required_concepts: A definition reference is a specified source or generated occurrence linked to a qualified definition or candidate definitions.
The link may use syntax, name binding, imports, attribute access, type information, or runtime identity.
The record distinguishes a resolved link from a conservative candidate link.
The record preserves confidence and ambiguity in the relation.
major_error_concepts: Calling every textual spelling match a semantic reference to the same definition.

cards.prompt: Define Definition source retrieval. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The attempt to recover source text and location for a recorded runtime object using documented inspection interfaces, with wrappers, generated code, interactive definitions, built-ins, missing source, and retrieval exceptions recorded.
required_concepts: Definition source retrieval is an attempt to recover source text and location for a recorded runtime object.
The attempt uses documented inspection interfaces under a specified environment.
The result records wrapper and generated-code relationships.
The result records interactive definitions, built-ins, missing source, and retrieval exceptions when encountered.
major_error_concepts: Treating unavailable source as proof the object has no implementation.

cards.prompt: Define Dependency-group inclusion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A standardized group entry incorporating another named dependency group into the expanded requirement list, with normalization, cycles, duplicate retention, order, and tool handling considered.
required_concepts: A dependency-group inclusion is a standardized entry that incorporates another named group into an expanded requirement list.
Group-name normalization applies while resolving the inclusion.
Expansion behavior records ordering and retention of duplicate requirements.
Expansion detects inclusion cycles and records the tool's failure or handling behavior.
major_error_concepts: Treating inclusion as copying a resolved or locked dependency graph.

cards.prompt: Define Development dependency group. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A named list in the standardized dependency-groups table for development or task-specific requirements not included in built distribution metadata as project dependencies merely by declaration.
required_concepts: A development dependency group is a named requirement list in the standardized dependency-groups table.
The group supports development or task-specific environments.
Merely declaring the group does not include its requirements as project dependencies in built distribution metadata.
major_error_concepts: Calling a dependency group an installable package extra for end users.

cards.prompt: Define Deprecated public name. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A still-supported public member marked for future removal or behavior change with replacement, notice mechanism, affected release range, and current compatibility status recorded.
required_concepts: A deprecated public name remains supported in the current release.
The deprecation marks the member for a future removal or behavior change.
The deprecation identifies the supported replacement.
The deprecation records how consumers are notified.
The deprecation records the affected release range.
The deprecation records the member's current compatibility status.
major_error_concepts: Calling a removed or silently broken name deprecated after compatibility has already ended.

cards.prompt: Define API deprecation boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The explicit release, audience, old behavior, replacement, warning channel, planned removal condition, and unpromised surfaces delimiting one deprecation claim.
