required_concepts: The explicit release, audience, old behavior, replacement, warning channel, planned removal condition, and unpromised surfaces delimiting one deprecation claim.
major_error_concepts: Announcing vague future change with no affected identity or replacement path.

cards.prompt: Define Direct callee. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A qualified callable object or candidate set selected by one call site after binding, lookup, dispatch, and wrapper relations are considered, with runtime observation and static possibility kept distinct.
required_concepts: A direct callee is the qualified callable or candidate set selected by one call site.
Callee selection accounts for binding, lookup, dispatch, and wrapper relations.
The callee record distinguishes a runtime-observed target from a statically possible target.
major_error_concepts: Naming the syntactic attribute as a unique callee without dispatch evidence.

cards.prompt: Define Direct caller. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A specified function, method, module body, entry wrapper, or generated unit containing a call site confirmed or conservatively linked to a target callable under specified static or runtime evidence.
required_concepts: A direct caller is a specified executable unit containing a call site linked to the target callable.
The executable unit may be a function, method, module body, entry wrapper, or generated unit.
The caller relation records whether its support is confirmed or conservative.
The caller relation records the static or runtime evidence used for the link.
major_error_concepts: Calling a module a direct caller when the actual call lives in an unreached nested function.

cards.prompt: Define Direct change consumer. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A specified import, call, construction, subclass, protocol use, configuration reader, metadata consumer, check, documentation path, or entry wrapper directly dependent on a changed target field under admitted evidence.
required_concepts: A direct change consumer is an admitted surface that immediately depends on a changed contract field.
The surface may be an import, call, construction, subclass, protocol use, configuration reader, or metadata consumer.
The surface may instead be a check, documentation path, or entry wrapper.
The dependency relation remains bounded to the admitted navigation evidence.
major_error_concepts: Counting files instead of the exact dependency relation each consumer uses.

cards.prompt: Define Direct import edge. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** One evidence-backed importer-to-target relation caused by a specific reached import request, annotated with source site, condition, execution phase, result, and whether the target was newly initialized or cached.
required_concepts: A direct import edge is an evidence-backed relation from one importer to one target.
The edge is caused by a specific import request that was reached.
The edge records the request's source site.
The edge records the condition under which the request was reached.
The edge records the execution phase.
The edge records the request result.
The edge records whether the target was newly initialized or supplied from cache.
major_error_concepts: Treating every syntactic import as reached in every execution.

cards.prompt: Define Discovered check-module identity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A candidate source path successfully mapped and imported under a qualified name for check loading, with origin, cache prestate, import effects, and loading errors preserved.
required_concepts: A discovered check-module identity begins with a candidate source path.
The path is successfully mapped to a qualified module name.
The module is successfully imported for check loading.
The record preserves the selected module origin.
The record preserves module-cache prestate and import-time effects.
The record preserves loading errors associated with discovery.
major_error_concepts: Counting a matching filename before proving which module object was imported.

cards.prompt: Define unittest discovery filename pattern. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The versioned filename matching rule used to select candidate check modules during discovery, distinct from test-method name rules and from successful import or collection.
required_concepts: A unittest discovery filename pattern is a versioned matching rule for candidate check modules.
The pattern selects candidate filenames during discovery.
The filename pattern is distinct from test-method naming rules.
Matching the pattern does not prove successful module import or case collection.
major_error_concepts: Assuming all Python files beneath the discovery root are collected.

cards.prompt: Define unittest discovery start directory. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The versioned filesystem location from which recursive check discovery begins, interpreted with a top-level directory, importability rules, pattern, working directory, and package structure.
required_concepts: A unittest discovery start directory is a versioned filesystem location where recursive discovery begins.
Discovery interprets that location with a declared top-level directory.
Discovery applies the relevant importability rules.
Discovery applies a declared filename pattern.
Discovery records the process working directory.
Discovery records the package structure used to derive module identities.
major_error_concepts: Reporting discovery results without preserving the start and top-level directories.

cards.prompt: Define unittest discovery top-level directory. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The versioned directory used to derive importable module names for discovered files and inserted or interpreted for import resolution, with source-tree identity and shadowing risks explicit.
required_concepts: A unittest discovery top-level directory is versioned.
The directory is used to derive importable module names for discovered files.
The directory is inserted or interpreted for import resolution according to runner semantics.
The directory is bound to an identified source tree.
The configuration records import-shadowing risks.
major_error_concepts: Deriving module identity from the discovery start directory alone.

cards.prompt: Define Distribution project identity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The metadata-defined installable project name and version used by packaging tools and installed-distribution records, kept distinct from repository name, project root, and import names.
required_concepts: Distribution-project identity is the metadata-defined installable project name and version.
Packaging tools use that identity.
Installed-distribution records use that identity.
Distribution-project identity is distinct from the repository name and project-root path.
Distribution-project identity is distinct from the project's import names.
major_error_concepts: Deriving the installed distribution name from an import statement.

cards.prompt: Define Doctest ellipsis matching. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** An option allowing a marker in expected output to match any substring, increasing tolerance while potentially hiding meaningful values, ordering, exceptions, or omitted evidence.
required_concepts: Doctest ellipsis matching allows a marker in expected output to match any substring.
The option increases matching tolerance.
Doctest ellipsis tolerance can hide meaningful values, ordering, exceptions, or omitted evidence.
major_error_concepts: Replacing most expected output with ellipses and calling the example verified.

cards.prompt: Define Doctest example. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A discovered interactive-style source example with prompts, executable input, expected output, option flags, namespace, source location, and runner context interpreted by doctest matching rules.
required_concepts: A doctest example is a discovered interactive-style source example.
The example records prompt text.
The example records executable input.
The example records expected output.
The example records option flags.
The example records the execution namespace.
The example records its source location.
The example records runner context.
The runner interprets the example under doctest matching rules.
major_error_concepts: Treating every code block in documentation as an automatically collected doctest.

cards.prompt: Define Doctest exception example. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** An interactive-style example whose expected output describes an exception traceback under doctest matching rules, with exception class and selected detail preserved but traceback formatting limits explicit.
required_concepts: A doctest exception example is an interactive-style example whose expected output describes an exception traceback.
The runner compares the traceback under doctest matching rules.
The expectation preserves the exception class and selected details.
The expectation states limits on traceback-format matching.
major_error_concepts: Accepting any exception merely because expected output contains the word traceback.

cards.prompt: Define Doctest expected output. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified text representation expected after an example executes, compared through doctest's selected normalization and option behavior rather than object equality or semantic result comparison.
required_concepts: Doctest expected output is a specified text representation expected after an example executes.
The runner compares the text using selected doctest normalization and option behavior.
The comparison is not ordinary Python object equality.
The comparison does not automatically establish semantic equality of results.
major_error_concepts: Calling matching displayed text proof that hidden object state is correct.

cards.prompt: Define Duplicate log emission. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** Multiple output emissions derived from one record because overlapping handlers, repeated configuration, propagation, or accidental multiple logging calls route it more than intended under the configured topology.
required_concepts: A duplicate log record is multiple unintended emissions attributable to one logical logging event.
Duplication may arise from overlapping handlers, repeated configuration, enabled propagation, or repeated logging calls.
The configured logger-handler topology and logging-call count distinguish possible duplication mechanisms.
major_error_concepts: Deduplicating text after emission without repairing the routing mechanism.

cards.prompt: What boundary or limitation does Dynamic-dispatch analysis limit impose?
cards.definition:
**Definition.** The unresolved callee possibilities introduced by runtime types, protocols, inheritance, descriptors, registries, callbacks, entry points, plugins, computed names, or monkey patching beyond admitted static and runtime evidence.

**Worked check.** A call through `getattr(obj,name)` with input-derived `name` may be invisible to a closed static call graph; bound the reported graph to resolved targets.
required_concepts: A dynamic-dispatch analysis limit records unresolved callee possibilities beyond the admitted evidence.
Uncertainty may arise from runtime types, protocols, inheritance, descriptors, registries, or callbacks.
Entry points, plugins, computed names, and monkey patching may add further candidates.
The limit separates statically possible and runtime-observed dispatch from unexamined alternatives.
major_error_concepts: Collapsing an open extension surface to the single implementation observed once.

cards.prompt: Define Dynamic import request. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A module request whose target name or timing is computed at runtime through an import interface rather than fixed entirely by ordinary import-statement syntax.
required_concepts: A module request whose target name or timing is computed at runtime through an import interface rather than fixed entirely by ordinary import-statement syntax.
major_error_concepts: Omitting computed imports from impact analysis because no matching import statement exists.

cards.prompt: What does dynamic project metadata delegate to the build backend, and can an eligible dynamic field include static entries under PEP808?
cards.definition: A field listed in project.dynamic delegates determination of its final metadata to the backend. Under PEP808/current PyPA rules, eligible list/table fields may include static entries as an append-only starting portion; the backend may add but not remove, reorder or modify those entries. Scalar fields do not gain this exception. The chosen backend must support the adopted rules, and final values require artifact readback.
required_concepts: Dynamic marks backend participation in final metadata; it need not mean every entry is absent from pyproject.
Eligible list/table static portions can coexist under PEP808 with append-only preservation, subject to backend support; do not extend this to scalars.
accepted_variants: A supported backend can extend a dependencies list that has static entries and is also listed in dynamic, preserving those entries. The final list still needs backend readback; this PEP808 exception does not allow both static and dynamic scalar version values.
major_error_concepts: Every dynamic field must have no static entries under current rules, or the backend may freely replace static entries once dynamic is listed.

cards.prompt: Define Effective configuration value. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The value selected for one schema field after source parsing, conversion, precedence, merge, and validation, paired with winning provenance and shadowed candidates rather than detached from its resolution history.
required_concepts: An effective configuration value is the selected value for one field after parsing, conversion, precedence, merge, and validation.
The value records the source provenance that won selection.
The effective configuration value is paired with lower-precedence candidates that were shadowed.
major_error_concepts: Logging only the final value and making configuration disputes impossible to audit.

cards.prompt: Define Effective logger level. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The threshold obtained from a logger's explicit level or nearest configured ancestor according to hierarchy rules, evaluated before handler thresholds and other filtering.
required_concepts: A logger's effective level is its explicit level or the nearest explicit ancestor level found through inheritance.
The effective level participates in deciding whether a logging call creates a record.
The effective logger-level decision occurs before handler-level and filter decisions.
major_error_concepts: Reading only the child's level field and predicting record emission.

cards.prompt: Define Import-safe main function. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A callable entry boundary that accepts specified arguments or dependencies, performs application work only when invoked, returns an application status, and can be imported without automatically running that work.
required_concepts: An import-safe main function is a callable application-entry boundary.
The function accepts specified arguments or injected dependencies.
The function performs application work only when invoked.
The function returns an application status.
Importing the function's module does not automatically invoke that application work.
major_error_concepts: Hiding global argument reads and process exit inside import-time code while naming another wrapper `main`.

cards.prompt: Define Distribution entry-point group. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A consumer-defined namespace collecting installed entry points for one discovery purpose, with group naming, collision policy, accepted object interface, and security limitations defined by that consumer.
required_concepts: A distribution entry-point group is a consumer-defined namespace for one discovery purpose.
The consumer defines valid group naming and the accepted interface of loaded objects.
The consumer defines collision handling among records in the group.
The consumer defines security limitations for discovering and loading group entries.
major_error_concepts: Assuming every entry-point group creates an executable shell command.

cards.prompt: Define Distribution entry-point record. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The installed metadata triple of group, name, and object reference plus distribution provenance, optional extras, and parsed module and attribute components used for discovery and loading.
required_concepts: A distribution entry-point record stores an installed group, name, and object reference.
The record retains provenance to its owning distribution.
The record may include optional extras associated with loading.
The record exposes parsed module and attribute components for discovery and loading.
major_error_concepts: Loading an entry-point object before recording its owning distribution and collision context.

cards.prompt: Define Environment installed-distribution inventory. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The declared set of distribution names, versions, metadata locations, files where available, requirements, entry points, and import-name mappings visible to one environment interpreter.
required_concepts: An environment installed-distribution inventory is observed through one selected environment interpreter.
The inventory records distribution names, versions, and metadata locations.
The inventory records installed files when that metadata is available.
The inventory records declared requirements and installed entry points.
The inventory records mappings from distribution names to import names when available.
major_error_concepts: Treating declared project dependencies as evidence of what is actually installed.

cards.prompt: Define Environment interpreter selection. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The explicit executable path or resolved command that selects a virtual environment's Python for one invocation, kept distinct from shell activation and directory naming.
required_concepts: Environment interpreter selection records the explicit executable path or resolved command used for one Python invocation.
The selected executable determines which virtual environment's interpreter is invoked.
Interpreter selection is distinct from modifying a shell through activation.
Interpreter selection is distinct from the name of the directory containing the environment.
major_error_concepts: Assuming the command `python` resolves to the intended environment because its prompt looks activated.

cards.prompt: Define Dependency environment marker. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A standardized Boolean condition over declared environment properties controlling whether a requirement applies in a target context, with variables, comparison semantics, extras context, and evaluated result recorded.
required_concepts: A dependency environment marker is a standardized Boolean condition over declared environment properties.
The marker determines whether its requirement applies in a selected target context.
The marker record includes referenced variables and comparison semantics.
The marker record includes any extras context and the evaluated Boolean result.
major_error_concepts: Treating a marker as a runtime conditional import inside application code.

cards.prompt: Define Environment configuration conversion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The explicit parsing of a selected environment string into the schema-required value kind with accepted spellings, empty handling, errors, provenance, and no inference from annotation alone.
required_concepts: Environment-value conversion explicitly parses an environment string into a configuration-schema value kind.
The conversion contract declares accepted spellings and the treatment of empty strings.
The conversion contract declares errors for malformed values.
The converted value retains provenance to its environment key.
Type annotations alone do not infer environment-value conversion behavior.
major_error_concepts: Calling `bool(environment_text)` a reliable parser for Boolean configuration values.

cards.prompt: Define Equality assertion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** An assertion applying equality semantics and runner-provided diagnostics to specified expected and observed objects, distinct from identity, approximate numeric relation, membership, ordering, and representation equality.
required_concepts: An equality assertion applies equality semantics to specified expected and observed objects.
The runner supplies diagnostics for an equality mismatch.
Equality is distinct from identity, approximate numeric relation, membership, ordering, and representation equality.
major_error_concepts: Using equality where aliasing or object identity is the actual requirement.

cards.prompt: Define Error check-case result. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A selected case whose setup, body, or cleanup raises an exception outside the runner's assertion-failure classification, with phase, traceback, partial observations, and remaining lifecycle behavior recorded.
required_concepts: An error check-case result belongs to a selected case whose setup, body, or cleanup raised an exception outside assertion-failure classification.
The result records the lifecycle phase that raised.
The result records the traceback.
The result records partial observations made before the error.
The result records remaining lifecycle behavior after the error.
major_error_concepts: Combining errors with failed expectations and losing whether the unit was exercised.

cards.prompt: What does Exception-bearing log record diagnose or distinguish?
cards.definition:
**Definition.** A log record carrying captured exception information for formatter rendering, kept distinct from raising, reraising, swallowing, handling, returning an error code, or changing application state.

**Worked check.** Inside `except`, `logger.exception('load failed')` records message plus active traceback; logging only `str(exc)` loses type and call path.
required_concepts: An exception log record carries captured exception information for later formatter rendering.
Creating the record is distinct from raising, reraising, swallowing, or otherwise handling the exception.
Creating the record does not by itself return an application status or change application state.
major_error_concepts: Calling `logger.exception` recovery or proof that the error was handled safely.

cards.prompt: Define Module execution-identity matrix. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A row-per-launch-mode comparison of selected source, qualified identity, `__name__`, `__package__`, `__spec__`, search-path lead, cache relation, arguments, effects, return, and process exit for one project release.
required_concepts: A module execution-identity matrix has one row for each launch mode under comparison.
Each row records the selected source artifact.
Each row records the qualified module identity.
Each row records the values of `__name__`, `__package__`, and `__spec__`.
Each row records the leading module-search-path entry.
Each row records the relation to the module cache.
Each row records the program arguments.
Each row records observable effects.
Each row records the application return value.
Each row records the process exit outcome.
All rows refer to the same identified project release.
major_error_concepts: Comparing only printed output and calling execution identities equivalent.

cards.prompt: Define Exhaustiveness assertion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A statically typed call or construct placed at an intended impossible remainder so a checker reports newly unhandled union or literal members when the control-flow partition ceases to be exhaustive.
required_concepts: An exhaustiveness assertion is placed in the control-flow remainder intended to be impossible.
A checker reports newly unhandled union or literal members at that assertion.
The report appears when the preceding control-flow partition is no longer exhaustive.
major_error_concepts: Treating exhaustiveness evidence as proof every runtime input was validated into the declared closed set.

cards.prompt: Define Expected-exception assertion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A bounded executable observation requiring a selected operation to raise a compatible exception type, optionally checking message or attributes, while failing if no exception or an incompatible exception occurs.
required_concepts: An expected-exception assertion requires one selected operation to raise a compatible exception type.
The assertion may additionally check the exception message or attributes.
The assertion fails if the operation raises no exception.
The assertion fails if the operation raises an incompatible exception.
major_error_concepts: Wrapping multiple operations so an earlier unrelated exception satisfies the case.

cards.prompt: Define Expected-failure case result. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A case marked as known failing whose observed failure is classified specially by the runner, retaining the unresolved defect rather than converting it into passed behavior.
required_concepts: An expected-failure case is marked as known failing before execution.
The runner classifies its observed failure specially.
The special classification retains the unresolved defect.
Expected-failure classification does not convert failing behavior into a passing observation.
major_error_concepts: Reporting expected failures as green evidence that the requirement is satisfied.

cards.prompt: Define Explicit relative import. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** An import request whose leading-dot level and package context determine an absolute qualified target without consulting the current working directory as a sibling shortcut.
required_concepts: An explicit relative import is identified by a leading-dot level.
The request's package context supplies its resolution anchor.
The leading-dot level and package context determine an absolute qualified target.
Explicit relative-name resolution does not use the current working directory as a sibling-import shortcut.
major_error_concepts: Treating leading dots as filesystem `../` traversal independent of module package identity.

cards.prompt: Define Explicit variable annotation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A source declaration constraining or documenting the intended static type of a binding under checker rules while leaving assignment execution and runtime value acceptance unenforced by default.
required_concepts: An explicit variable annotation is a source declaration of an intended static binding type.
A configured checker may use the declaration as a constraint.
The annotation does not prevent assignment execution at runtime by default.
The annotation does not reject a runtime value by default without separate validation.
major_error_concepts: Treating a variable annotation as object conversion or runtime storage allocation.

cards.prompt: Contrast module-cache cleanup after a failed initial import with a failed reload. Are earlier effects rolled back?
cards.definition: A failed initial import removes the failing module's newly inserted sys.modules entry while preserving modules successfully loaded as side effects. A failed reload leaves the existing module in sys.modules; its namespace may already be partly changed. Neither behavior transactionally undoes previous side effects.
required_concepts: Initial-loading failure removes the failing module entry, not all successfully loaded dependencies.
Reload failure retains the existing cached module and may leave partial updates; effects are not automatically undone.
accepted_variants: Failed first import removes its failing module, leaving successful dependencies cached. A failed reload leaves the old module object cached, potentially partly updated. Earlier side effects are not automatically rolled back.
major_error_concepts: Every failed import or reload removes the module and all dependencies, restoring the process exactly to its previous state.

cards.prompt: Define Assertion-failure case result. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A selected case in which an assertion records an unmet expected-observed relation, with source location, comparison details, preceding effects, and later cleanup outcome preserved.
required_concepts: An assertion-failure result belongs to a selected case whose assertion found an unmet expected-observed relation.
The result preserves the assertion source location.
The result preserves comparison details.
The result preserves effects that occurred before the failure.
The result preserves the outcome of later cleanup.
major_error_concepts: Calling every unsuccessful case an assertion failure regardless of exception phase.

cards.prompt: What does Codebase file-role classification denote, including its domain or type when relevant?
cards.definition:
**Definition.** The evidence-backed assignment of each versioned path to source, check, configuration, metadata, resource, generated, documentation, build output, vendored, cache, unknown, or multiple roles without inferring behavior solely from extension.

**Worked check.** Classify `src/pkg/api.py` as runtime source and `tests/test_api.py` as test code using repository policy; an extension alone cannot distinguish generated or vendored files.
required_concepts: A file-role classification assigns each versioned path one or more evidence-backed roles.
Admitted roles include source, check, configuration, metadata, resource, generated, documentation, build output, vendored, cache, and unknown.
A path may retain multiple roles when the evidence supports multiple functions.
The classification does not infer behavior solely from a filename extension.
major_error_concepts: Assuming every `.py` file is handwritten runtime application source.

cards.prompt: Define Static final name. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A typing declaration directing compatible checkers to reject later reassignment of a binding under specified scopes while leaving runtime rebinding technically possible unless separately prevented.
required_concepts: A static final-name declaration directs compatible checkers to reject later reassignment within the specified scopes.
The restriction is a static checker rule.
Runtime rebinding remains technically possible unless a separate runtime mechanism prevents it.
major_error_concepts: Describing `Final` as immutable storage or a security boundary.

cards.prompt: Define Finder-cache invalidation request. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A request for participating finders to invalidate location caches after importable resources may have changed, without clearing loaded modules or guaranteeing discovery of a target.
required_concepts: A finder-cache invalidation request asks participating finders to invalidate location caches after importable resources may have changed.
Finder-cache invalidation does not clear already loaded modules from the module cache.
Finder-cache invalidation does not guarantee that a requested target will be discovered.
major_error_concepts: Treating cache invalidation as module reload or environment reset.

cards.prompt: Define Import finder identity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The frozen import-system participant queried to locate a specification for a requested module name under a particular path and target context.
required_concepts: The frozen import-system participant queried to locate a specification for a requested module name under a particular path and target context.
major_error_concepts: Conflating the component that locates a module specification with the loader that initializes the module.

cards.prompt: Define Forward annotation reference. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** An annotation reference to a type name not yet ordinarily available at the source evaluation point, represented and resolved according to the specified annotation mode and tool context.
required_concepts: A forward annotation reference names a type not yet ordinarily available at the annotation's source evaluation point.
The specified annotation mode determines how the reference is represented.
The annotation mode and tool context determine how the reference is later resolved.
major_error_concepts: Fixing every forward reference by adding an eager runtime import that creates a cycle.

cards.prompt: Define Frozen dataclass boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The generated restriction on ordinary attribute assignment and deletion for a dataclass instance, which does not recursively freeze referenced mutable objects or create absolute immutability.
required_concepts: A frozen dataclass generates a restriction on ordinary attribute assignment.
The generated restriction also covers ordinary attribute deletion.
Freezing the dataclass does not recursively freeze mutable objects referenced by its fields.
The generated restriction does not create absolute immutability.
major_error_concepts: Claiming `frozen=True` makes the complete reachable object graph immutable.

cards.prompt: Define Static function type signature. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The checker-interpreted parameter and return types, generic variables, overload context, and callable compatibility of one function release, kept separate from runtime argument binding and behavioral contracts.
required_concepts: A static function type signature records checker-interpreted parameter types.
The signature records the checker-interpreted return type.
The signature records scoped generic variables.
The signature records relevant overload context.
The signature participates in static callable-compatibility judgments.
The static signature is distinct from runtime argument binding.
The static signature is distinct from the function's behavioral contract.
major_error_concepts: Replacing the API input, exception, effect, and ownership contract with annotations alone.

cards.prompt: What boundary or limitation does Generated-code navigation boundary impose?
cards.definition:
**Definition.** The explicit relation among generator source, generator version and inputs, produced path and hash, checked-in or build-time status, runtime use, and safe edit authority for one generated artifact.

**Worked check.** A generated client file is excluded from manual edits but included in package checks; change the generator input, regenerate, and verify the diff rather than patching output by hand.
required_concepts: A generated-code navigation boundary links a generated artifact to its generator source and version.
The boundary records generator inputs and the produced path and content hash.
The boundary records whether the output is checked in or produced during a build.
The boundary records runtime use of the generated artifact.
The boundary identifies the authority and safe edit location for changing generated behavior.
major_error_concepts: Treating generated output as ordinary owned source or ignoring it entirely in impact analysis.

cards.prompt: Define Dataclass generated-initializer contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The version- and option-bound parameter order, kinds, defaults, assignments, inheritance contributions, and post-initialization call exposed by the dataclass-generated `__init__`.
required_concepts: A dataclass generated-initializer contract is bound to a Python version and decorator options.
The contract records generated parameter order.
The contract records parameter kinds.
The contract records defaults.
The contract records generated field assignments.
The contract records contributions inherited from dataclass bases.
The contract records the post-initialization call exposed by the generated `__init__`.
major_error_concepts: Assuming field declaration order always yields a legal or unchanged constructor across inheritance.

cards.prompt: Define Generic class. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A class parameterized by one or more types so constructor, attributes, and methods can maintain specified static relations across instances without altering ordinary runtime validation by default.
required_concepts: A generic class is parameterized by one or more types.
The class can relate constructor types to the selected parameters.
The class can preserve parameter relations across attributes and methods.
Generic-class static relations can differ across parameterized instances.
Generic parameterization does not automatically add runtime value validation.
major_error_concepts: Treating each parameterized class spelling as an automatically enforcing runtime container class.

cards.prompt: How are a generic Python function's type parameters selected at a call, and is f[int](...) ordinary supported function-call syntax in Python 3.14?
cards.definition: A generic function relates input and output types through scoped type parameters. Compatible checkers infer their values from call arguments and context, subject to bounds/constraints. In Python3.14, an ordinary generic function is not subscripted as f[int](...); explicit generic-class specialization is a different mechanism.
required_concepts: Scoped type parameters express static input/output relations and are inferred under checker constraints.
Do not treat f[int](...) as ordinary supported generic-function invocation in Python3.14.
accepted_variants: A checker infers type arguments from the call and context while enforcing bounds. For def identity[T](x:T)->T, identity(1) is an ordinary call; identity[int](1) is not the supported way to explicitly specialize this function in Python3.14.
major_error_concepts: Every generic function accepts explicit type arguments with f[int](...), just like a generic class.

cards.prompt: Define Generic static instantiation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The substitution of concrete type arguments for a generic declaration's parameters at an annotation or inferred use site, subject to arity, bounds, constraints, defaults, and checker rules.
required_concepts: Generic static instantiation substitutes concrete type arguments for a generic declaration's parameters.
The substitution occurs at an annotation or inferred use site.
The substitution must satisfy parameter arity.
The substitution must satisfy declared bounds and constraints.
Declared defaults are used only where supported and applicable.
The configured checker's generic rules govern the resulting instantiation.
major_error_concepts: Treating generic instantiation as construction of a runtime object instance.

cards.prompt: Define Generic variance relation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The declared or inferred rule governing how subtype relations among type arguments induce assignability among corresponding generic instantiations, classified as covariant, contravariant, or invariant for one parameter.
required_concepts: Generic variance is the declared or inferred rule for one generic type parameter.
The rule determines how subtype relations among type arguments induce assignability among generic instantiations.
The parameter is classified as covariant, contravariant, or invariant under that rule.
Variance is evaluated for the specified generic interface and parameter.
major_error_concepts: Assuming every generic preserves the same subtype direction as its type argument.

cards.prompt: Define Handler threshold decision. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The handler-specific severity comparison applied after a record reaches that handler, allowing different destinations to accept different subsets independently from the originating logger threshold.
required_concepts: A handler-threshold decision compares a reached record's severity with the handler's configured level.
Different handlers may therefore emit different subsets of the same routed records.
The handler-threshold decision is independent of the earlier logger-threshold decision.
major_error_concepts: Treating one global logging level as the only threshold in the route.

cards.prompt: What does bounded API idempotence require for successive identical calls on state, and why are equal return values insufficient?
cards.definition: For fixed arguments and a declared observation boundary, an idempotent state operation has the same relevant effect when repeated on its own result as when applied once: F(F(s)) is observationally equivalent to F(s) on the admitted states. The second call is not preceded by resetting s. Logging or other excluded effects must be explicitly outside the claim; return values need not be identical.
required_concepts: Compare sequential F(F(s)) with F(s) without resetting state between those two calls.
State the relevant effect/observation boundary; equal return values alone do not establish idempotence.
accepted_variants: Set enabled=True twice has the same relevant final state as once. Increment-and-return-0 twice changes the counter twice despite equal returns. Compare sequential effects without resetting, within the stated observation boundary.
major_error_concepts: Returning 0 on every call proves idempotence even if each successive call increments persistent state.

cards.prompt: Define Identity assertion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** An assertion that expected and observed references denote the same runtime object or differ in identity, with equality and immutable-object interning effects kept outside the claim.
required_concepts: An identity assertion asks whether expected and observed references denote the same runtime object or differ in identity.
Object equality remains outside the identity claim.
Immutable-object interning can affect observed identity and remains outside a value-equality inference.
major_error_concepts: Using identity assertions for ordinary numeric or text value equality.

cards.prompt: Define a strongly connected component of a directed import graph and specify when that component actually contains a directed cycle.
cards.definition: An SCC is a maximal group of vertices that are mutually reachable. A component contains a cycle if it has at least two vertices, or if its lone vertex has a self-loop. An isolated singleton is an SCC but not a cyclic component. A static cyclic component alone does not prove a runtime import failure.
required_concepts: An SCC is maximal under mutual reachability, relative to the chosen graph.
Cyclic components have more than one vertex or a singleton self-loop; an ordinary singleton need not be cyclic.
accepted_variants: An SCC is a maximal mutually reachable group. Two or more vertices imply a cycle; a singleton needs a self-loop. One isolated module is an SCC but not an import cycle.
major_error_concepts: Every strongly connected subset is a whole component, and every singleton SCC necessarily contains an import cycle.

cards.prompt: Define Import dependency direction. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The declared higher-to-lower or interface-to-implementation relation used to decide which module may import which other module in one bounded package design.
required_concepts: The declared higher-to-lower or interface-to-implementation relation used to decide which module may import which other module in one bounded package design.
major_error_concepts: Applying an architectural slogan without mapping actual qualified modules and consumers.

cards.prompt: Define Python import-dependency graph. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A Python import-dependency graph has qualified module identities as nodes and direct import relations as edges for a declared static or runtime observation scope, with conditional, dynamic, failed, cached, and unobserved relations distinguished.
required_concepts: A Python import-dependency graph uses qualified module identities as nodes.
The graph uses direct import relations as edges.
The graph declares whether its observation scope is static, runtime, or a named combination of the two.
The graph distinguishes conditional relations.
The graph distinguishes dynamically generated relations.
The graph distinguishes failed and cache-satisfied relations.
The graph distinguishes relations that remain unobserved in the declared scope.
major_error_concepts: Calling a static syntax scan the complete runtime import graph.

cards.prompt: Define Import-package-to-distribution mapping. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** Version-bound installed-metadata evidence relating top-level import package names to distribution projects while allowing zero, one, or multiple candidates rather than assuming a bijection.
required_concepts: An import-package-to-distribution mapping is bound to an identified installed-environment version.
The mapping uses installed metadata as evidence relating top-level import package names to distribution projects.
A top-level import name may map to zero, one, or multiple candidate distributions.
The mapping does not assume a bijection between import packages and distribution projects.
major_error_concepts: Claiming a one-to-one mapping from identical or similar spellings.

cards.prompt: Define Import-time effect inventory. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The ordered record of bindings, registrations, environment reads, resource access, logs, stream writes, mutations, and failures caused by importing each public path in a fresh recorded process.
required_concepts: An import-time effect inventory is ordered by the import trace for each supported public path.
The inventory records any bindings, registrations, environment reads, resource accesses, logs, stream writes, mutations, or failures caused by import.
Each public path is inspected in a fresh recorded process.
major_error_concepts: Recording only external I/O and omitting global registrations or environment-dependent bindings.

cards.prompt: Define Python import environment. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A Python import environment comprises the interpreter, working directory, launch mode, import hooks, module search path, module cache state, installed distributions, and relevant environment values governing an import request.
required_concepts: A Python import environment identifies the interpreter handling the import request.
The import environment records the working directory.
The import environment records the program launch mode.
The import environment records installed import hooks.
The import environment records the ordered module search path.
The import environment records the relevant module-cache state.
The import environment records installed distributions.
The import environment records environment values that can govern import resolution.
major_error_concepts: Reproducing source files while leaving the module cache, search path, and installed distributions unspecified.

cards.prompt: Define Import error failure. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A specified failure in import processing or requested-name acquisition after considering whether a module was found, initialized, partially initialized, and actually supplied the named binding.
required_concepts: An import error failure is a specified failure in import processing or requested-name acquisition.
Diagnosis records whether the target module was found.
Diagnosis records whether the target module initialized or remained partially initialized.
Diagnosis records whether the module supplied the requested binding.
The recorded import states are considered before failure is attributed to search, initialization, or name acquisition.
major_error_concepts: Treating every `ImportError` as evidence that no module file exists.

cards.prompt: What does Import-failure localization diagnose or distinguish?
cards.definition:
**Definition.** The mapping from exception type, missing-name fields, traceback, active initialization chain, cache state, origin, and requested binding to the earliest unsupported import transition.

**Worked check.** A traceback ending in package `__init__` may originate in a transitive module. Record the first failing import and partially initialized modules, not only the caller's import line.
required_concepts: Import-failure localization records the exception type.
Import-failure localization records any missing-name fields.
Import-failure localization records the traceback.
Import-failure localization records the active module-initialization chain.
Import-failure localization records the relevant module-cache state.
Import-failure localization records the selected module origin.
Import-failure localization records the requested binding.
The evidence is mapped to the earliest unsupported transition in the import trace.
major_error_concepts: Selecting the last traceback frame as root cause without reconstructing the initialization chain.

cards.prompt: Define Import namespace binding. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The specific local or containing-package name-to-object relation established after import resolution, which varies across import forms and remains distinct from module creation or execution.
required_concepts: An import namespace binding is a specific name-to-object relation established after import resolution.
The relation may be established in a local namespace or in a containing package.
The binding produced depends on the import statement's form.
Namespace binding is distinct from module-object creation and module execution.
major_error_concepts: Assuming every imported qualified component becomes an independent local binding.

cards.prompt: Define Import package identity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A module object whose import specification supplies submodule search locations, enabling qualified descendants while remaining distinct from a distribution package or arbitrary directory.
required_concepts: An import package identity is a Python module object.
An import package identity has an import specification that supplies submodule search locations.
The package's submodule search locations enable qualified descendants of the package identity.
An import package identity is distinct from a distribution package.
An import package identity is distinct from an arbitrary directory.
major_error_concepts: Calling every directory containing Python files an import package.

cards.prompt: Define Import request. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** One runtime request for a named module relative to a specified package context, cache state, import environment, and from-list behavior before resolution and binding outcomes are known.
required_concepts: An import request is one runtime request for a named module.
The request records its package context.
The request records the relevant module-cache state.
The request records the import environment.
The request records its from-list behavior.
The import-request inputs are fixed before resolution and namespace-binding outcomes are known.
major_error_concepts: Describing only the final bound name and losing what qualified module was requested.

cards.prompt: Define Import-safe entry boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The demonstrated separation in which importing library definitions avoids application execution while explicit entry modes invoke the same specified callable contract with observable effects and exits recorded.
required_concepts: An import-safe entry boundary is demonstrated by importing library definitions without executing the application.
Explicit entry modes invoke the same specified callable contract.
The observable effects of each explicit entry mode are recorded.
The return value and process exit of each explicit entry mode are recorded.
major_error_concepts: Inferring import safety from source layout without executing a controlled import observation.

cards.prompt: Define Import search candidate. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A potential module or package contribution encountered for a requested qualified name at one ordered search location before finder acceptance, rejection, or namespace aggregation is recorded.
required_concepts: An import search candidate is a potential module or package contribution for a requested qualified name.
The candidate is associated with one ordered search location.
Candidate identity is recorded before the finder accepts it, rejects it, or aggregates it into a namespace package.
Acceptance, rejection, and namespace aggregation remain alternative finder outcomes.
major_error_concepts: Calling the first same-named path observed manually the selected import target without executing the specified search procedure.

cards.prompt: Define Import site. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A versioned source span that can issue an import request when reached, classified by form, resolved target or candidates, condition, execution phase, type-check-only status, and runtime observation.
required_concepts: An import site is a versioned source span that can issue an import request when execution reaches it.
The site record classifies the import form and resolved target or candidate targets.
The site record includes execution conditions and execution phase.
The site record distinguishes type-check-only use from runtime execution.
The site record reports whether the import request was observed at runtime.
major_error_concepts: Treating every import site as reached at process startup.

cards.prompt: Define Python import statement. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** Source syntax that issues one or more import requests and then performs specified namespace-binding operations, kept separate from the search and loading mechanisms it invokes.
required_concepts: A Python import statement is source syntax that issues one or more import requests.
After resolution, the statement performs the namespace-binding operations specified by its import form.
The import statement is distinct from the search and loading mechanisms that its requests invoke.
major_error_concepts: Treating an import statement as only file loading while omitting binding semantics.

cards.prompt: Define Import-time effect. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A binding, registration, stream write, file access, environment read, mutation, or other observation caused while resolving and initializing a module rather than by an explicit later API call.
required_concepts: An import-time effect can be a binding, registration, stream write, file access, environment read, mutation, or other observation.
An import-time effect occurs while a module is being resolved or initialized.
An effect caused only by an explicit later API call is not an import-time effect.
major_error_concepts: Calling imports declarative dependencies with no executable effects.

cards.prompt: Define Class inheritance relation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The runtime and interface relation in which a subclass derives attribute lookup, method resolution, construction interactions, and nominal type compatibility from one or more bases.
required_concepts: Class inheritance is both a runtime and an interface relation.
A subclass derives attribute-lookup behavior from its bases.
A subclass derives method-resolution behavior from its bases.
Base classes participate in subclass construction interactions.
Inheritance can confer nominal type compatibility.
Each inheritance claim is evaluated for the declared set of one or more base classes.
major_error_concepts: Using inheritance as code copying while ignoring public substitutability and method resolution.

cards.prompt: Define Installed distribution record. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The environment-bound metadata readback for one installed distribution including canonical lookup identity, declared name, version, files, requirements, entry points, and any missing or editable-install limitations.
required_concepts: An installed-distribution record is metadata read back from one identified environment.
The record includes the distribution's canonical lookup identity.
The record includes the declared distribution name.
The record includes the installed version.
The record includes the installed files when that metadata is available.
The record includes declared requirements.
The record includes declared entry points.
The record notes missing metadata that limits the readback.
The record notes editable-install behavior that limits identity claims.
major_error_concepts: Reading source-tree metadata and calling it evidence of what the active interpreter has installed.

cards.prompt: Define Installed entry-point readback. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The entry-point group, name, object reference, owning distribution, installed metadata location, selected target, collisions, and load result observed from the target environment.
required_concepts: Installed entry-point readback records the entry-point group, name, and object reference.
The readback records the owning distribution and installed metadata location.
The readback records target selection and any collisions among installed records.
The readback records the result or failure of loading the selected object.
major_error_concepts: Selecting the first same-named entry point while hiding other installed candidates.

cards.prompt: Define Installed import readback. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The target interpreter, working directory, import statement, module qualified name, origin, loader, distribution mapping, public bindings, effects, exception, and source-tree leakage checks after local artifact installation.
required_concepts: Installed import readback records the target interpreter, working directory, and executed import statement.
The readback records the module's qualified name, origin, loader, and distribution mapping.
The readback records public bindings and observable import effects.
The readback records any exception raised during import.
The readback checks for source-tree leakage after local artifact installation.
major_error_concepts: Calling an import successful without verifying which copy supplied the module.

cards.prompt: Define Installed package-resource readback. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified anchor, resource traversal, target environment, installed distribution, content bytes and hash, lifetime, and comparison with expected built artifact member for one packaged resource.
required_concepts: Installed resource readback specifies the package anchor and resource traversal used for selection.
The readback identifies the target environment and installed distribution.
The readback records selected resource bytes, their content hash, and access lifetime.
The observed resource is compared with the expected member of the built artifact.
major_error_concepts: Reading the source-tree resource and calling it installed-package evidence.

cards.prompt: Define Installed typing metadata. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The environment-bound stub packages, inline-typing markers, distribution versions, module mappings, and checker visibility that supply third-party type information for one analysis release.
required_concepts: Installed typing metadata is bound to one checker environment.
The metadata records installed stub packages.
The metadata records inline-typing markers.
The metadata records distribution versions.
The metadata records distribution-to-module mappings.
The metadata records which type information is visible to the checker.
major_error_concepts: Assuming an importable runtime package necessarily provides complete checker-visible types.

cards.prompt: Define Instance attribute. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A binding stored for one instance through its supported storage and assignment semantics, distinct from same-spelled class attributes and computed descriptors.
required_concepts: A binding stored for one instance through its supported storage and assignment semantics, distinct from same-spelled class attributes and computed descriptors.
major_error_concepts: Editing the class definition to explain state that exists only on one instance.

cards.prompt: Define Python instance object. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A runtime object whose type is a class and whose observable state combines instance-specific storage with class-mediated attribute lookup and behavior.
required_concepts: A runtime object whose type is a class and whose observable state combines instance-specific storage with class-mediated attribute lookup and behavior.
major_error_concepts: Assuming all attributes visible through an instance are stored on that instance.

cards.prompt: Define Python interface-choice matrix. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A consumer-bound comparison of plain functions, concrete classes, dataclasses, composition, inheritance, ABCs, and protocols across state, construction, static and runtime enforcement, extensibility, compatibility, and evidence costs.
required_concepts: A Python interface-choice matrix is evaluated for declared consumers.
The matrix compares plain functions, concrete classes, dataclasses, composition, inheritance, ABCs, and protocols as alternative interface forms.
The matrix compares state representation.
The matrix compares construction behavior.
The matrix compares static enforcement and runtime enforcement separately.
The matrix compares extensibility.
The matrix compares compatibility obligations.
The matrix compares the evidence cost of each choice.
major_error_concepts: Ranking language mechanisms universally without a consumer and change model.

cards.prompt: Define Internal Python name. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A reachable name intentionally outside the specified support contract whose use may still be technically possible and therefore is not secured or hidden by classification.
required_concepts: An internal Python name is intentionally outside the specified support contract.
An internal name may still be technically reachable.
Internal classification does not secure or hide the name.
Consumers that use the name do not thereby acquire the public compatibility promise.
major_error_concepts: Claiming consumers cannot import or access an internal name.

cards.prompt: Define Introspection side-effect risk. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The possibility that importing modules, retrieving members, resolving descriptors, unwrapping objects, or evaluating attributes during inspection executes code, mutates state, consumes resources, or raises exceptions.
required_concepts: Introspection side-effect risk arises because importing modules during inspection can execute code.
Retrieving members, resolving descriptors, unwrapping objects, or evaluating attributes can also execute code.
Inspection can mutate state, consume resources, or raise exceptions.
Introspection side-effect risk includes the possible execution, mutation, resource use, and exception outcomes of inspection.
major_error_concepts: Treating all inspection operations as passive reads of frozen metadata.

cards.prompt: What is isinstance-based static narrowing, and which runtime check forms and checker conditions govern it?
cards.definition: A checker may refine an expression's type along paths selected by a supported isinstance check. Python supports a class, a tuple of accepted types, and union types in modern releases. Actual static refinement depends on the original type, check form and checker configuration; runtime support alone does not promise identical narrowing in every checker.
required_concepts: It is checker-controlled, path-sensitive refinement after a supported isinstance test.
Supported runtime checks can include class, tuple and union inputs; checker support and the original static type still constrain refinement.
accepted_variants: An isinstance check can refine true/false paths under the checker rules. Modern Python accepts isinstance(x,int|str), as well as class and tuple forms; that runtime validity does not promise identical narrowing across checkers.
major_error_concepts: An isinstance test can never accept a union type as its second argument, and all runtime predicates narrow types identically.

cards.prompt: Define Isolated build environment. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A frontend-provisioned environment containing declared build requirements for one build operation, separated from ordinary project runtime dependencies while retaining tool, network, cache, and sandbox limitations.
required_concepts: An isolated build environment is provisioned by the frontend for one build operation.
The environment contains the declared build requirements needed to invoke the backend.
An isolated build environment's build requirements are separated from ordinary project runtime dependencies.
The environment retains the declared limitations of its tools, network, cache, and sandbox boundary.
major_error_concepts: Calling build isolation an operating-system sandbox or complete reproducibility guarantee.

cards.prompt: Define Isolated installation environment. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A newly created target virtual environment with specified base interpreter, empty or inventoried prestate, explicit artifact source, no project-root import leakage, and bounded commands for installation readback.
required_concepts: An isolated installation environment is a newly created target virtual environment with a specified base interpreter.
The environment has an empty or explicitly inventoried preinstallation state.
Installation uses an explicitly identified local distribution artifact as its source.
The environment prevents project-root import leakage under the selected invocation conditions.
The installation and readback commands are bounded and recorded.
major_error_concepts: Installing into the authoring environment and calling the result an isolated artifact test.

cards.prompt: Define Keyword-only parameter. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A specified parameter after the keyword-only boundary that requires an explicit keyword binding unless a default supplies it.
required_concepts: A specified parameter after the keyword-only boundary that requires an explicit keyword binding unless a default supplies it.
major_error_concepts: Assuming a parameter is keyword-only merely because documentation usually shows a keyword.

cards.prompt: Define Lazy result contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified boundary for a result whose computation, input reads, exceptions, or resource consumption occur during later iteration or access rather than entirely before the API returns.
required_concepts: A lazy result contract states which computation is deferred until later iteration or access.
The contract states which input reads and exceptions can occur during that later use.
The contract states which resources are consumed or retained during later use.
The API return boundary does not imply that all of those events occurred before the result object was returned.
major_error_concepts: Attributing an iteration-time exception to the initial call boundary.

cards.prompt: Define Leading-underscore interface convention. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The source-level naming convention signaling nonpublic intent and affecting some wildcard-import behavior without enforcing privacy or preventing explicit access.
required_concepts: A leading underscore is a source-level convention signaling nonpublic intent.
The convention affects some wildcard-import behavior.
A leading underscore does not enforce privacy.
A leading underscore does not prevent explicit access to the name.
major_error_concepts: Describing the leading underscore convention as an enforced access-control mechanism.

cards.prompt: Define Static literal type. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A static type restricted to one or more specific literal values, enabling value-sensitive checking and exhaustiveness while remaining distinct from runtime membership validation and unrestricted base types.
required_concepts: A static literal type is restricted to one or more specific literal values.
Literal types enable value-sensitive static checking.
Literal types support static exhaustiveness analysis.
A literal type does not automatically validate runtime membership.
A literal type remains distinct from its unrestricted base type.
major_error_concepts: Calling a literal annotation automatic runtime validation of external text.

cards.prompt: Define Import loader identity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The frozen object and class responsible for creating or executing a found module under its specification, with behavior bounded to the documented loader interface.
required_concepts: Import-loader identity records the exact loader object and its class.
The loader is responsible for creating or executing the found module under its specification.
Creation and execution are evaluated for the frozen import run.
The loader's claimed behavior is limited to its documented interface.
major_error_concepts: Assuming the standard source-file loader handles every imported module.

cards.prompt: Define Local static type inference. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The checker-specific derivation of an expression or binding type from source context, assignments, annotations, control flow, and configuration without executing the program.
required_concepts: Local static type inference is performed by the configured checker.
The checker derives a type for an expression or binding from source context.
The derivation uses assignments.
The derivation uses explicit annotations.
The derivation uses control-flow facts.
The derivation depends on checker configuration.
The checker derives the type without executing the program.
major_error_concepts: Calling an inferred type a measured runtime distribution of values.

cards.prompt: What boundary or limitation does Log-exception-exit boundary impose?
cards.definition:
**Definition.** The explicit separation among emitting a record, creating or catching an exception, returning an application code, and terminating a process, with each event's order and causal relation recorded.

**Worked check.** Logging an exception and returning exit 0 tells automation success. Either recover and prove the result or propagate/map the failure to a nonzero process status.
required_concepts: The log-exception-exit boundary separates emitting a log record from creating or catching an exception.
The boundary separates exception handling from returning an application status.
The boundary separates an application return status from terminating the process.
The execution contract records the order and causal relation among any of those events that occur.
major_error_concepts: Inferring control flow from the severity name of a log record.

cards.prompt: Define Log filter. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A logger- or handler-attached predicate or transformation participating in record acceptance and possible mutation under specified code, with order, state, effects, and exception behavior explicit.
required_concepts: A log filter is a logger-side or handler-side predicate or transformation applied to a record.
The filter contract declares whether records are accepted, rejected, or mutated.
The filter contract declares evaluation order, retained state, and side effects.
The filter contract declares behavior when filter evaluation raises an exception.
major_error_concepts: Treating filters as only severity thresholds or guaranteed privacy controls.

cards.prompt: What does Log formatter diagnose or distinguish?
cards.definition:
**Definition.** A handler-associated component converting accepted record fields into output text according to a specified format, style, time policy, exception rendering, and missing-field behavior.

**Worked check.** Given one log record, a text formatter and JSON formatter render different encodings but must preserve timestamp, level, logger, event, and exception fields required by the contract.
required_concepts: A log formatter converts an accepted record into handler output text.
The formatter contract declares the record fields and formatting style it expects.
The formatter contract declares time and exception rendering behavior.
The formatter contract declares the disposition of missing expected record fields.
major_error_concepts: Modifying formatting and claiming the underlying record severity or message changed.

cards.prompt: Define Log handler. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A configured destination component receiving propagated records, applying its own level and filters, formatting accepted records, and emitting to a stream, file, buffer, or other bounded target.
required_concepts: A log handler is a configured destination that receives a record routed through the logger hierarchy.
The handler applies its own level and filters to a received record.
The handler applies a selected formatter before emission when configured to do so.
The handler emits to its declared stream, file, buffer, or other destination.
major_error_concepts: Assuming attaching a handler guarantees every logger record reaches its destination.

cards.prompt: Define Logging severity level. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A numeric and named severity attached to a record or threshold, used in logger and handler filtering under configured configuration without automatically defining business impact or process exit.
required_concepts: A log level is a numeric severity value with an optional conventional name.
Record severity participates in logger-threshold and handler-threshold filtering.
A log level does not by itself measure business impact.
A log level does not determine the process exit status.
major_error_concepts: Equating every ERROR log with an exception or failed process.

cards.prompt: Define Log record propagation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The movement of a record from its originating logger to handlers attached along ancestor logger relationships while propagation remains enabled, with ancestor logger thresholds distinguished from handler processing.
required_concepts: Log propagation routes a record from its origin logger to ancestor handlers while propagation remains enabled.
Ancestor logger thresholds do not reapply to a record that has already been created.
Ancestor handler levels and filters still govern processing by those handlers.
major_error_concepts: Assuming every ancestor logger's level rechecks a record during propagation.

cards.prompt: What does Python logging `LogRecord` event diagnose or distinguish?
cards.definition:
**Definition.** The standard-library runtime event object produced by Python logging before formatting, carrying logger name, severity, message template, arguments, time, source context, exception information, and routing fields rather than an ML system's specified structured-event schema.

**Worked check.** Create one record with level, logger, message template, arguments, timestamp, and exception metadata; the rendered string is a view, not the complete record identity.
required_concepts: A log record is the standard logging event object created before handler formatting.
The record carries the logger name, severity, message template, and message arguments.
The record carries time, source-location, exception, and routing metadata when available.
A standard log record is distinct from an ML system's application-specific structured-event schema.
major_error_concepts: Treating the final displayed line as the complete original record.

cards.prompt: Define Logger name hierarchy. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The dot-separated ancestry relation among named loggers used for effective-level inheritance and record propagation, distinct from Python package ownership despite often following module names.
required_concepts: A logger hierarchy is the dotted-name ancestry used for effective-level inheritance and record propagation.
